job.title: General Manager Housing Operations
job.description:
About YWCA Australia
YWCA Australia is a national, purpose led organisation supporting women, gender diverse people and their families to achieve safety, stability and long-term housing security.

YWCA’s Housing & Property function operates across Victoria, Queensland, New South Wales, South Australia and the Northern Territory, supporting more than 550 tenancies and over 800 residents. With a growing housing portfolio and significant development activity underway, YWCA Australia is continuing to strengthen its housing operations and capability.

Guided by its values of Striving for Equality, Acting from the Heart and Working Better Together, this is an opportunity for an experienced housing leader to create lasting impacts that are more than houses.

Grounded in an intersectional feminist approach, YWCA Australia’s work goes beyond delivering housing, but to also support the creation of homes by its residents, as well as creating safe, stable and thriving communities that will ultimately also shape the future direction of a growing national Housing & Property function.

About the Role
The General Manager, Housing Operations is a key leadership role within YWCA Australia’s Housing & Property function, reporting to the Director, Development and Housing. The General Manager, Housing Operations is also a contributing member of the organisation’s Senior Leadership Team.

Leading three direct reports and a broader team of approximately 15 people, the role will provide national leadership across housing operations spanning five jurisdictions, with accountability for operational performance, service excellence, resident outcomes, regulatory compliance and continuous improvement.

A key focus will be strengthening the capability, consistency and maturity of the Housing Operations function as it continues to evolve. You will lead and develop the team, build the values-based culture that promotes accountability, collaboration and resident-centred practice.

Through your leadership, the Housing Operations function will continue to build capability, strengthen systems, processes and practices, and deliver high quality and compliant housing services, that create positive outcomes for residents and communities.

The role will play a critical role in delivering positive resident outcomes and shaping organisational success through:
  • National Housing Operations and resident management
  • Resident engagement and outcomes
  • Leading and embedding a values-based, inclusive and resident-centred culture across Housing Operations
  • Operational performance, governance and risk
  • Community housing regulatory compliance
  • Systems, technology and continuous improvement across the function
  • Strategic partnerships with government, regulators and sector stakeholders
  • Business planning, budgeting and performance reporting.
This position requires someone who can operate comfortably between the operational and strategic. You will need to understand and lead and manage the realities of frontline Housing Operations, while also having the leadership maturity to operate above the day-to-day to support your leadership team and drive broader organisational priorities.

A key to success will be working closely with the General Manager, Property and broader organisational stakeholders, all of whom contribute to integrated housing outcomes and future growth across operations, property, asset management, maintenance, advocacy, marketing and communications, people and culture, technology, finance, governance, etc.

About You
You are an experienced and values led housing leader with a strong understanding of community housing and the realities of delivering resident centred services within complex environments.

You are motivated by the opportunity to create positive outcomes for residents and communities and are committed to leading with authenticity, empathy and accountability.

You will ideally bring:
  • Significant senior leadership experience across community housing, social housing, homelessness or a related human services environment
  • A demonstrated ability to build engaged, high-performing teams and foster a culture of collaboration, inclusion and continuous improvement
  • Experience leading multi-site or geographically dispersed teams
  • Strong understanding of housing operations and regulatory requirements, including the National Regulatory System for Community Housing (NRSCH) and relevant state based frameworks
  • Proven capability across operational performance, budgets, governance, risk and compliance
  • Strong commercial, analytical, strategic and technological capability
  • Experience building relationships with government, regulators, funders and community stakeholders.
Importantly, you are a genuine people leader who understands the importance of supporting those working closest to residents and communities. You bring a collaborative, supportive and practical leadership style, are comfortable leading complexity and change, and are motivated by improving housing outcomes for women, gender diverse people and their families.

National housing experience will be highly regarded, however YWCA Australia is open to candidates who may not have operated at a national level, provided they bring the right combination of housing expertise, leadership capability, attitude and willingness to step into a broader remit. YWCA recognises that diverse career pathways can bring valuable perspectives and approaches to the work.

Salary: $167,500 - $170,000 + superannuation + NFP salary packaging benefits.


Application Process
For a confidential discussion or to receive a copy of the Candidate Information Pack, please contact:  Sarah Kettlewell on 0478 041 199 or sarah@publicsectorpeople.com.au.

Public Sector People are partnering exclusively with YWCA Australia on this appointment. All applications and enquiries will be managed by Public Sector People.

job.title: A07 Workforce Analyst
job.description:
Public Sector People are working with a QLD State Government Department who are seeking an experienced Workforce Analyst on a temp contract until the end of December with opportunity to extend.
  
Overview:
  
  • ASAP START | AO7 Workforce Analyst
  • Attractive pay rates from $87 p/h + 12% Super (PAYG)
  • Brisbane Northern suburbs
  • Initial contract until end of December with opportunity to extend to March 2027
  • WFH up to two days per week (pending performance)
  
What's involved

Workforce Strategy and Analytics delivers workforce strategy, planning, and analytic services that contribute to achieving a highly capable, contemporary, and connected workforce.  The Workforce Analytics unit has a primary function to deliver staff and establishment reporting and data to meet departmental and external requirements.
   
Responsibilities will include but not be limited to:
  
  • Transform this data into descriptive, predictive, and interactive analytics that offer workforce insights, to support the department’s executive decision-making and strategic workforce planning.
  • Manage the research, analysis and preparation of high quality workforce information and reporting in line with departmental and external reporting requirements to meet the needs of key stakeholders.
  • Manage and ensure workforce data governance, including audit recommendations, security and other control mechanisms in the delivery of data and reporting products to ensure accurate information. 
  • Provide high level advice, with data driven insights, on a range of strategic HR issues and support the development of key strategies and priorities to build workforce capacity and capability.
 What we are looking for:
  • Government experience and available with 1 week notice
  • The ideal candidate for this role would have had leadership experience. Although there are no direct reports, this role is a senior position in the workforce analytics team and would benefit with a degree of exposure or direct experience in leadership capabilities.

  • Experience in managing data extraction and analysis, and presenting workforce information (i.e. staff, payroll, establishment data) for decision-making in a large complex organisation.
  
***This is a competitive role and the client is moving fast ***
  
As an approved Government recruitment partner Public Sector People are ideally placed to assist you in your search for your next temporary or permanent opportunity. 
   
Best of luck!

job.title: Estimating Manager
job.description:
About the Company
A well-established residential building business based in Hamilton, Brisbane, is looking for an experienced Estimating Manager to take ownership of its estimating program.

Estimating sits at the centre of the business, with projects priced from in-house designs, quantity take-offs, supplier and trade rates. The business operates through a fully integrated Databuild and Onsite Companion workflow system.

With the current Estimating Manager moving on, this is an opportunity for an experienced estimator to step into a key position, take ownership of the estimating function and build on the systems already in place.

About the Role
As the Estimating Manager, you will take ownership of the estimating program while remaining hands-on with the day-to-day estimating function.
You will prepare take-offs, budgets and estimates, manage supplier and trade pricing, identify cost-saving opportunities and lead and mentor the estimating team.

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, you will work closely with the construction, operations and product development teams to ensure projects are accurately priced, cost-effective and aligned with the company's objectives.
This is a key role for someone who is committed, reliable and enthusiastic, with a strong focus on accuracy, efficiency, profitability and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
  • Operate and maintain the integrated Databuild system, including cost codes, catalogues and pricing databases.
  • Maintain the flow of data between Databuild and Onsite Companion.
  • Prepare and review accurate quantity take-offs, bills of quantities and Job Analysis Reports.
  • Conduct technical plan reviews at both Preliminary Plans and Working Drawings stages.
  • Prepare detailed cost estimates for customer proposals, factoring in general and special conditions.
  • Ensure sales estimates meet required budgets and deadlines.
  • Develop scopes of works for external stakeholders.
  • Review supplier and subcontractor quotations and negotiate pricing to identify cost-saving opportunities.
  • Prepare project budgets for management approval and monitor actual costs against budget.
  • Report on project progress, costs and profitability to management.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Ensure subcontractor licences and insurances are current and accurately recorded in Onsite Companion.
  • Lead, mentor and support the estimating team.
  • Assist with internal projects and business initiatives as required.
About You To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • 5+ years' experience in construction estimating, ideally within residential building.
  • Strong, hands-on experience with Databuild, including operation, administration and maintaining pricing databases and cost codes.
  • Strong knowledge of cost estimation, bills of quantities and material take-offs.
  • Experience conducting technical plan reviews at Preliminary Plans and Working Drawings stages.
  • Experience preparing detailed budgets and analysing supplier and subcontractor quotations.
  • Strong understanding of subcontractor compliance, including licensing and insurance requirements.
  • Excellent negotiation and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • A highly analytical, organised and detail-oriented approach.
  • The ability to identify cost savings without compromising quality.
  • A proactive and results-driven approach, with a focus on process improvement.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and changing priorities.
  • Relevant qualifications in construction management, quantity surveying or estimating, or equivalent industry experience.
Our Systems Hands-on Databuild experience is essential. The successful candidate will be trained on the other systems where required.
  • Databuild – Construction estimating, job costing and accounting.
  • Onsite Companion – Site and project management, linked with Databuild.
  • Therefore – Document management and invoice approval workflow.
The Opportunity This is an opportunity to step into a key position within a growing residential building business and have genuine ownership over the estimating function.

You will have the opportunity to lead an established estimating team, work directly with the Managing Director and contribute to improving systems, processes and profitability across the business.

If you are an experienced residential estimator with strong Databuild experience and are ready to take the next step into an Estimating Manager position, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now with your CV, or contact us for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Controls/PLC Engineer
job.description:
Controls / PLC Engineer — Major Materials Handling Infrastructure Project

Employer: A global leader in automated logistics and materials handling systems
Location: Western Sydney (on-site during project phases)
Project: Large-scale automated materials handling systems as part of a major infrastructure development

About the Role Our client, a global leader in automated logistics and materials handling systems, is looking for a Controls/PLC Engineer to join the team delivering critical automation systems for a major infrastructure project in Western Sydney. This is a rare opportunity to work on one of the region's most significant infrastructure builds, with long-term career runway as the project moves from installation through commissioning and into live operations.

You'll be responsible for the design, programming, testing, and commissioning of PLC-based control systems that drive automated baggage handling — critical, high-availability systems where reliability and safety are non-negotiable.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design, develop, and commission PLC and SCADA control systems for large-scale automated materials handling equipment
  • Program and configure using Siemens PLC platforms (S7, TIA Portal, WinCC or equivalent)
  • Support system integration, testing, and commissioning across a major site's automated handling infrastructure
  • Troubleshoot and resolve control system faults during commissioning and post-handover support phases
  • Collaborate with mechanical, electrical, and project engineering teams to ensure systems meet performance and safety requirements
  • Produce and maintain technical documentation, including control philosophies, I/O lists, and functional specifications
  • Support continuous improvement and reliability initiatives as the system transitions into live operation
About You
  • Degree qualified in Electrical, Electronic, Mechatronic, or Controls Engineering (or equivalent trade + experience pathway)
  • Proven hands-on experience with Siemens PLC programming (S7-300/400/1500, TIA Portal) — essential
  • Experience with SCADA/HMI systems (WinCC or similar)
  • Background in materials handling, conveyor systems, or large-scale automated logistics systems highly regarded
  • Comfortable working on a live, high-profile infrastructure project with strict safety and quality standards
  • Strong fault-finding and commissioning experience — able to work through complex control system issues under pressure
  • Excellent communication skills, able to liaise across engineering, project management, and client stakeholders
Why Apply
  • Be part of the team delivering critical automation systems for a brand-new, large-scale infrastructure project — genuine legacy project experience
  • Work with a global benchmark name in automated logistics and materials handling
  • Long-term career pathway as the project moves from delivery into ongoing operations and support
  • Exposure to large-scale Siemens-based automation systems, sought after across major logistics and infrastructure projects globally

job.title: Coordinator Infrastructure Planning and Development
job.description:
About Melton City Council

Melton City Council is one of Australia’s fastest-growing municipalities, located in Melbourne’s thriving western growth corridor. With significant population growth and infrastructure investment underway, Council is focused on ensuring the right infrastructure is planned and delivered at the right time to support its rapidly growing communities.
  
This growth creates an exciting opportunity for an experienced infrastructure planning professional to play a key leadership role in shaping Melton’s long-term infrastructure priorities and future investment.
  
About the Role

Reporting to the Manager City Infrastructure Planning, you will lead a multidisciplinary team responsible for shaping Melton’s long-term infrastructure planning and development.
  
A key focus will be coordinating and continually improving Council’s long-term capital works pipeline, bringing together growth forecasts, infrastructure priorities, financial considerations and project readiness to support confident investment decisions.
  
Working across Council, you will take a strategic view of future infrastructure needs, ensuring projects are appropriately planned, prioritised and aligned with Council’s broader financial and asset planning. You will work closely with capital works, community, open space, recreation and transport[AJ1]  planning, development contributions and other internal teams to understand the bigger picture and help determine what infrastructure is required, when it is needed and how it can be delivered.
  
The role also has significant external influence, building relationships and negotiating with State Government, developers, statutory authorities and service agencies around major roads, rail, schools, community infrastructure, utilities and other infrastructure required to support population growth.
  
You will also oversee strategic land acquisition activities and contribute to the ongoing improvement of infrastructure planning, governance and decision-making across Council.
  
In return, Melton City Council offers a genuinely flexible and supportive working environment, including:
  • 5 weeks annual leave
    • 13 ADOs per annum
    • Genuine flexible work options and hybrid working arrangements
    • Extensive Career Development & Leadership Programs
    • Access to the Local Government Employee Health Plan (GMHBA) with exclusive benefits
    • 16 weeks Paid Parental Leave (superannuation paid during parental leave)
    • 3 weeks Paid Secondary Carer Leave
    • Wellbeing initiatives
  
About You

You are an experienced infrastructure planning professional who combines strong strategic thinking with the people and stakeholder skills required to operate across a complex growth environment.
  
You will bring a strong understanding of infrastructure planning, ideally gained within local government, consulting, State Government or a comparable environment. Experience across growth area planning, capital works planning, asset management, development contributions or strategic infrastructure investment will be highly regarded.
  
An understanding of Council budgeting and the relationship between capital works, long-term financial planning and asset management will enable you to confidently assess priorities and support long-term investment decisions.
  
Importantly, this role requires a strong people leader. You will be collaborative and approachable, with the ability to develop a capable team, manage performance and create clarity around priorities and expectations.
  
Strong communication and influencing skills will be essential, along with the ability to simplify complex information, build trusted relationships and bring different stakeholders together around long-term infrastructure outcomes.
  
Tertiary qualifications in engineering, project management, strategy, business management or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Melton City Council to recruit this opportunity on behalf of the City Infrastructure Planning team.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
  
Applications close Monday 28th September 2026.

job.title: Coordinator Infrastructure and Public Realm
job.description:
COORDINATOR INFRASTRUCTURE AND PUBLIC REALM
  
About Moonee Valley City Council

Moonee Valley City Council is a diverse and vibrant municipality in Melbourne’s inner north-west, delivering a broad range of services and infrastructure that support the safety, amenity and everyday experience of the community.
  
Council is focused on delivering high-quality, responsive and sustainable services while ensuring its infrastructure assets are effectively maintained, renewed and managed for the long term.
  
This position presents an exciting opportunity to provide leadership across Council’s Infrastructure and Public Realm operations and help shape the future delivery of these important community services.
  
About the Role

The Coordinator Infrastructure and Public Realm is a newly created senior position responsible for the delivery of Council’s road and public infrastructure maintenance services, ensuring assets are safe, compliant, well maintained and delivering value for the community.
  
Reporting to the Manager City Presentation, you will lead a multidisciplinary team and function spanning roads and footpaths, drainage, playground infrastructure, signage and line marking, public realm assets and infrastructure inspections.
  
A key focus will be leading Council’s Road Management Plan obligations, alongside the planning and delivery of minor infrastructure renewal programs, ensuring effective inspection, defect management, compliance, prioritisation and delivery.
  
You will provide strong leadership across people, contractors, budgets and service performance, while working collaboratively across Council to drive continuous improvement, strengthen service delivery and ensure infrastructure services respond to organisational and community priorities.
  
About You

You are an experienced infrastructure leader with a strong background in road and public infrastructure maintenance, ideally gained within Local Government or a similarly complex service delivery environment.
  
Your technical knowledge spans civil infrastructure maintenance and renewal, supported by a sound understanding of statutory inspection regimes, the Road Management Act and risk-based approaches to infrastructure maintenance.
  
Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary operational teams, managing contractors and budgets, and coordinating infrastructure maintenance and minor capital renewal programs will be important to your success in the role.
  
You are comfortable balancing competing operational priorities while making sound decisions around safety, risk, service levels, asset performance and community expectations.
  
Importantly, you are a collaborative and pragmatic leader who can build capability within your team, establish strong relationships across the organisation and drive continuous improvement in the way services are planned and delivered.
  
A tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline is essential.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Moonee Valley City Council to recruit this newly created opportunity within the City Presentation department.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.

The key is being someone who can take ownership of a project and drive it forward.
Project Experience The ideal candidate will have experience across:
  • Apartments

High-end residential experience is not required. The focus is on practical, larger-scale residential and social housing projects.

You will also have exposure to working with government authorities, planning requirements, building codes and relevant approval processes, particularly across social housing developments.

job.title: Head of Parks and Urban Forest
job.description:
HEAD OF PARKS AND URBAN FOREST
  
About Moonee Valley City Council

Moonee Valley City Council is a diverse and vibrant municipality in Melbourne’s inner north-west, delivering a broad range of services that support the amenity, environment and everyday experience of the community.
  
Council is focused on delivering high-quality, responsive and sustainable services while continuing to strengthen how its operations are planned, managed and delivered.
  
This position presents an exciting opportunity to lead one of Council’s largest operational functions and shape the future delivery of its parks, open space and urban forest services.
  
About the Role
  
The Head of Parks and Urban Forest is a senior position responsible for the planning and delivery of Council’s sports fields, conservation, parks, cityscapes and tree services, ensuring high standards of presentation, amenity, safety and environmental performance.
  
Reporting to the Manager City Presentation, you will oversee a large multidisciplinary operational function, with responsibility for developing capability, strengthening performance and creating a positive and accountable team culture. With much of the service delivered in-house, a key priority will be strengthening workforce planning, scheduling and resource allocation to support efficient and responsive service delivery.
  
The role will take a broader view of how the function operates, identifying opportunities to improve systems, processes and service performance while building capability and accountability across the team. You will also oversee budgets and key contracts, balancing operational priorities with safety, service quality and value for the community.
  
Working collaboratively across Council and with community stakeholders, you will help ensure these highly visible services continue to respond to organisational priorities, environmental outcomes and community expectations.
  
About You
  
You are an experienced operational leader with a background across parks, trees, open space, sports grounds or a related service environment. Experience at Coordinator level or above within Local Government, or in a similarly complex service delivery environment, will be highly regarded.
  
Importantly, you will bring strong people management capability, with experience overseeing sizeable and diverse operational teams. You know how to build capability, set clear expectations and create a culture of accountability, safety and high performance, while confidently managing change and addressing performance when required.
  
You bring the ability to step beyond day-to-day operational requirements and look at the bigger picture, identifying opportunities to improve workforce planning, resource allocation, scheduling and the way services are delivered.
  
Commercial and financial capability will also be important, with experience managing budgets, contractors and resources and making considered decisions around service quality, cost and value.
  
A collaborative and pragmatic approach will be key. You will be comfortable building strong relationships across Council, engaging with the community and bringing people with you as the function continues to evolve.
  
A relevant tertiary qualification directly related to the portfolio is required, with postgraduate qualifications in business management or a related discipline viewed favourably.
  
Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Moonee Valley City Council to recruit this newly created opportunity within the City Presentation department.
  
For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.
  
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.
Applications close at 5pm Tuesday 29th September 2026.

This is a strong opportunity for an experienced project professional who enjoys variety and wants greater ownership across the complete project lifecycle.

Rather than being limited to one asset class or one stage of delivery, you will work across multiple infrastructure portfolios and partner closely with Council's asset owners, consultants, contractors and internal stakeholders.

Ideally, you will bring:

The Central Highlands is one of Queensland's major regional economies and offers the opportunity to build your career while contributing to infrastructure that has a visible impact on communities across the region.

For the right person, the attraction goes beyond an individual project. You will have the opportunity to:

job.description:
Partnering with one of Perth's more established civil contractors who've played an integral part amongst some of the cities key landmarks and developments, they are looking to bring onboard a surveyor with three years of local surveying experience, that is wanting to join a team that likes to have fun, and someone who enjoys the relationships that are built out on site. This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of a respected name, with genuine work life balance, and opportunity to work with flexibility and autonomy, whilst having a direct line for support if required. 

The Role: 
As the Surveyor managing the projects located in Perth's southern suburbs, you'll be allocated across four projects, conducting field surveys, set out works, processing surveying data, and working with engineers, supervisors and clients to support construction progress. 

Key Responsibilities:
  • Conduct field surveys for construction and infrastructure projects
  • Set out works in accordance with design drawings and specifications
  • Operate and maintain surveying equipment (total stations, GPS, levels)
  • Interpret engineering plans and provide clear data to site teams
  • Record and process survey data accurately for reporting and design purposes
  • Liaise with engineers, supervisors, and clients to support construction progress
  • Ensure all survey work complies with safety and quality standards
Requirements:
  • Minimum of three years local surveying experience.
  • Relevant qualifications in surveying or civil engineering. (Desirable).
  • Proficient with survey instruments and software (e.g. AutoCAD, 12d, CivilCAD).
  • Experience using Trimble surveying equipment and technology.
  • Strong understanding of civil construction processes and site operations.
  • Excellent attention to detail and spatial awareness.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a site based team.
  • WA C Class Driver’s Licence.
What’s on Offer:
  • Salary: Starting from $100,000 + Superannuation (Dep on Exp.)
  • Vehicle: Fully maintained company vehicle, with fuel card & laptop.
  • Genuine Work/Life Balance: Monday to Friday
  • Flexible: Flexible start times, with a 45 hour working week.
  • Team: Enjoyable team culture, with support and mentorship from senior surveyors. 
  • Be Recognised: Not just another number, but part of the team and family valued business; Have fun, have a laugh and be celebrated.
  • Company Events: Site BBQ's and half yearly company events. 
If you feel your experience matches the person specification please contact click apply. For any questions about the role, please contact Reece Saldaris at Reece@designandbuild.com.au or 0431 555 104.

The ideal candidate will have experience delivering change across Finance and ERP environments, with experience working with TechnologyOne (TechOne) highly desirable. A strong understanding of the local government environment will also be highly regarded.

You will work closely with the Manager Transformation, project teams and senior leaders to develop and implement change strategies that support employee adoption, minimise resistance and ensure people are ready for upcoming changes.

Key responsibilities:

  • Plan and coordinate change activities including communications, stakeholder engagement, training and transition planning
  • Undertake change impact assessments and readiness assessments across the organisation
  • Identify and engage key stakeholders to support successful adoption
  • Develop and monitor change success measures and report progress through governance forums
  • Support the development of clear and engaging change communications
  • Work closely with Digital and ICT project teams to integrate change activities into project plans
  • Provide advice, support and coaching to senior leaders, managers and supervisors
  • Establish and embed change management practices across Council
About you:
  • Minimum 5 years' experience in organisational change management across complex programs or projects
  • Strong knowledge of change management principles, methodologies and tools
  • Experience working across the full change lifecycle, from planning through to implementation and adoption
  • Experience delivering change within Finance and/or ERP environments
  • Experience with TechnologyOne (TechOne) is highly desirable
  • Strong understanding of, or experience working within, a local government environment
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, influencing and relationship-building capabilities
  • Ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of an organisation
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
  • Experience working within both Agile and Waterfall project environments
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint
  • Change management certification or formal qualification is desirable
The opportunity:
  • 1 Month Short-term contract
  • Eastern suburbs location
  • Flexible working arrangements available
  • Opportunity to contribute to significant Digital and ICT transformation initiatives

job.title: Reporting Lead
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced and commercially focused Reporting Lead to drive reporting, analytics, and automation capabilities across the organisation. This role will lead the design, development, automation, and optimisation of enterprise reporting solutions while partnering with senior business leaders to deliver actionable insights that support strategic decision-making.

The successful candidate will combine deep technical expertise in Power BI, SQL, Microsoft Fabric, and report automation with exceptional stakeholder management skills. You will be responsible for transforming complex business requirements into scalable reporting and analytics solutions that improve visibility, performance, and decision-making across the business.

This is an opportunity to lead the evolution of a modern reporting function, leveraging Microsoft's data and analytics platform to build enterprise-grade, automated reporting capabilities.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the organisation's reporting and analytics capability, ensuring reliable, scalable, and business-focused reporting solutions.
  • Design, develop, and maintain enterprise-grade dashboards, reports, and visualisations using Power BI.
  • Develop and optimise datasets, semantic models, and reporting architectures using SQL and modern data platform technologies.
  • Leverage Microsoft Fabric to support data integration, transformation, governance, analytics, and reporting initiatives.
  • Lead the automation of reporting processes to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and increase reporting timeliness.
  • Design and implement automated data pipelines, report refresh schedules, alerting mechanisms, and report distribution processes.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline reporting workflows and eliminate manual reporting activities across the organisation.
  • Partner with senior executives and business leaders to understand strategic objectives, reporting requirements, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Translate complex business requirements into technical reporting and analytics solutions.
Skills & Experience Essential
  • Extensive experience in a Reporting Lead, BI Lead, Analytics Lead, or similar senior reporting role.
  • Advanced expertise in Power BI, including:
    • Data modelling
    • DAX
    • Power Query
    • Dashboard and report development
    • Performance optimisation
  • Strong hands-on experience with SQL for data extraction, transformation, and analysis.
  • Proven experience working with and implementing solutions within Microsoft Fabric environments.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering report automation and enterprise reporting solutions.
  • Strong understanding of automated reporting processes, data orchestration, scheduling, and workflow optimisation.
  • Experience automating data ingestion, transformation, reporting, and dashboard refresh processes.
  • Exceptional senior stakeholder management skills, including the ability to engage, influence, and challenge executive stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to gather requirements, define reporting strategies, and translate business needs into technical solutions.
Desirable
  • Experience with Azure Data Platform technologies.
  • Knowledge of data governance, data quality, and reporting frameworks.
  • Experience leading reporting, analytics, or business intelligence teams.
  • Relevant Microsoft certifications in Power BI, Fabric, Data Analytics, or Azure.
  • Experience supporting self-service reporting and analytics initiatives.
What Success Looks Like
  • A trusted advisor to senior leadership on reporting, analytics, and data strategy.
  • Delivery of accurate, timely, and impactful business insights.
  • Significant reduction in manual reporting through automation and process improvement.
  • Increased adoption and maturity of Power BI and Microsoft Fabric capabilities.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and measurable business outcomes driven by data.
  • Improved reporting governance, efficiency, scalability, and data quality across the organisation.
Interested in exploring? Apply now! Interviews will be commencing soon.

job.title: A08 Operations Manager (Owners Representative)
job.description:
This QLD State Government department is seeking an experienced Operations Manager (Owner’s Representative) to provide operational leadership, governance and assurance for a first-of-its-kind critical minerals processing facility.

Acting as the Queensland Government’s on-site representative, you will play a key role in building strong relationships, aligning multiple stakeholders and creating a high-performing operational environment as the facility progresses through commissioning and into early operations.

This is a highly collaborative role requiring an experienced leader who can work effectively with operators, contractors, technical specialists, government stakeholders and customers. The ability to influence, communicate clearly and build trust across diverse groups will be critical to success.

Key Responsibilities
  • Act as the Owner’s Representative, building strong relationships and translating owner, contractor and customer requirements into clear operational expectations.
  • Provide visible operational leadership and establish a positive culture of accountability, collaboration and performance.
  • Establish and maintain the operational governance and assurance framework for early operations.
  • Build effective working relationships across operators, contractors, suppliers, advisors, government stakeholders and customers.
  • Drive performance through structured governance, reporting, communication and decision-making processes.
  • Influence outcomes across multiple organisations and stakeholder groups, including where there is no direct line authority.
  • Lead operational and campaign readiness reviews and provide recommendations for go/no-go decisions.
  • Foster strong operating discipline, performance routines and timely close-out of actions and commitments.
  • Provide on-site oversight of high-risk activities and ensure critical controls are effectively implemented.
  • Monitor operational performance and work collaboratively with stakeholders to identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities.
  • Chair performance, defect and improvement forums to drive accountability, collaboration and operational availability.
  • Provide high-quality advice, briefings and recommendations to senior stakeholders and government representatives.
  • Support commercial activities including contract development, procurement and broader stakeholder engagement.
  • Maintain robust Management of Change (MOC) processes and support sound asset management and reliability practices.
Successful Candidate
Leadership & People Management
  • Significant experience in operations leadership, operational management, Owner’s Representative or operational assurance roles within complex industrial, resources, minerals processing or similarly high-risk environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead, influence and engage people across multiple teams, organisations and professional disciplines.
  • Proven ability to establish a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety and high performance.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build trust and credibility with operators, contractors, technical specialists, senior executives and government stakeholders.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and bringing diverse stakeholders together to achieve common operational outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes without relying solely on direct line authority.
Operational & Industry Experience
  • Experience supporting commissioning, start-up or early operations of processing, resources, infrastructure or other complex industrial facilities.
  • Strong understanding of operational governance, risk management, Management of Change and operational assurance principles.
  • Experience in minerals, resources, processing or related heavy industry environments is highly desirable, but not essential for the right operational leader.
  • Practical experience verifying critical controls and making sound, risk-based operational decisions.
  • A strong understanding of operational performance, reliability and continuous improvement.
Stakeholder & Commercial Skills
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with a broad range of stakeholders and prepare clear reports, advice and briefings for senior decision-makers.
  • Proven ability to develop and maintain productive relationships across multiple organisations and stakeholder groups.
  • Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills, with the ability to resolve issues and maintain alignment in a complex environment.
  • Commercial acumen and experience with contract management, procurement and supplier relationships.
  • Strong project management and operational planning capability.
  • Ability to analyse information, identify opportunities and drive improvements in an evolving operational environment.
Qualifications & Requirements
  • Current open C Class Driver Licence.
  • Construction White Card.
  • Australian citizenship, permanent residency or valid work rights in Australia.
  • Willingness to travel as required.
  • Ability to successfully complete criminal history and conflict of interest checks.
This role offers a unique opportunity for an experienced operations and people leader to play a key role in establishing and governing operations for a strategically important critical minerals facility.

You will have the opportunity to work across government, industry and technical stakeholders while helping establish the culture, relationships and operating framework for a new facility that will contribute to Queensland’s growing advanced manufacturing, resources and critical minerals sector.

job.title: Supervisor Operational Maintenance
job.description:
Supervisor Operational Maintenance
Mackay Regional Council | Parks & Open Spaces | Level 5
  
Public Sector People are partnering with Mackay Regional Council to appoint a Supervisor Operational Maintenance — a hands-on leadership role responsible for planning and delivering maintenance activities and project outcomes across Council’s built infrastructure and facilities.
  
This is an opportunity for an experienced facilities, building maintenance, asset or trade professional to step into a broad supervisory role combining team leadership, maintenance planning, minor project delivery, contractor management and technical advice.
  
The Role
  
Reporting to the Coordinator Building Maintenance, you will lead the operational maintenance function and supervise the Facilities Operation Officer and Team Leader Operational Maintenance. You will coordinate reactive and preventative maintenance, minor capital and operational projects, and support the long-term performance of Council’s built assets.
  
Your responsibilities will include:
  
  • Planning, scheduling and coordinating maintenance activities across Council’s built infrastructure and facilities
  • Leading the delivery of minor capital and operational projects from scoping through to completion
  • Conducting building condition assessments and using condition data to inform planned maintenance and asset renewal priorities
  • Developing project scopes, cost estimates and resource requirements
  • Managing contractors, trades, suppliers and service providers, including contractual and WHS compliance
  • Supporting contract renewals and improving contractor performance and service delivery
  • Monitoring expenditure and contributing to annual financial performance across managed assets
  • Providing practical technical advice on building and facility maintenance to internal stakeholders and external contractors
  • Leading, motivating and developing staff while maintaining a strong safety, wellbeing and accountability culture
  
The position also participates in a rostered on-call function, with some out-of-hours work and domestic travel required.
  
About You
  
You will be a practical and organised maintenance or facilities professional who understands how to keep a diverse built asset portfolio operating safely, efficiently and reliably. Just as importantly, you will be comfortable leading people, coordinating competing priorities and working closely with contractors and internal stakeholders.
Council is open to candidates from facilities management, building maintenance, asset management, project delivery or relevant trade backgrounds.
  
You will bring:
  
  • Demonstrated experience delivering reactive and preventative maintenance across buildings or facilities
  • Experience scoping, planning, scheduling and delivering minor capital and operational projects
  • Strong contractor, trade and supplier management capability
  • Experience with building condition assessments, maintenance planning and asset renewal activities
  • The ability to read and interpret building plans, specifications and engineering reports
  • Sound knowledge of relevant building, fire safety and workplace health and safety requirements
  • Strong team leadership, communication, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills
  • Confidence using corporate systems, Microsoft Office and asset/facility management software
  
Relevant qualifications in Project Management, Facilities Management, Building Maintenance, Asset Management, a trade or another related field are required. A Diploma is preferred, although Certificate III/IV qualifications or substantial relevant experience may also be considered. A General Construction White Card and Queensland C Class Driver Licence, or interstate equivalent, are essential.
  
Previous local government experience will be highly regarded but is not essential.
  
Why Join Mackay Regional Council?
  
This role offers the opportunity to take ownership of a highly visible operational maintenance function within one of Queensland’s major regional councils. You will work across a diverse portfolio of community infrastructure and have the scope to improve maintenance planning, contractor performance, asset information and day-to-day service delivery.
  
Mackay combines the career opportunities and infrastructure of a major regional centre with a coastal lifestyle, strong
community identity and easy access to beaches, national parks and the Whitsundays.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply please hit the ‘Apply now’ button attaching your CV and a cover letter or for more information contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Consultant – Public Sector People
adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Application deadline: Thursday 17th September at 4pm

job.title: Senior Airport Operations & Compliance Coordinator
job.description:
Senior Airport Operations & Compliance Coordinator

Fraser Coast Regional Council | Hervey Bay, QLD | Airport Operations | Stream A Level 6 $104,018 | 9-Day Fortnight | Relocation Assistance up to $6,000

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Fraser Coast Regional Council to recruit a Senior Airport Operations & Compliance Coordinator — a key operational leadership role supporting the safe, secure and compliant operation of Council's airports.

Reporting directly to the Airport Manager, this position will act as a key 2IC within the Airport team, leading an experienced operational team while taking ownership across airside operations, aviation safety, security, compliance and emergency preparedness.

The Role

This is far more than a traditional airport operations position.

You'll play a critical role in ensuring Council's airports continue to meet their operational and regulatory obligations while having the opportunity to make the role your own, establish improved systems and help shape how the airport manages its compliance responsibilities into the future.

A major initial focus will be reviewing and strengthening the airport's compliance framework, ensuring key manuals, procedures and regulatory requirements remain current while establishing a clear ongoing system for managing compliance activities and critical dates.

Working closely with the Airport Manager, you'll lead and support a team of four Airport Operations Officers and an Airport Operations & Business Support Officer, while providing specialist advice across airside operations, safety, security and regulatory compliance.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading and coordinating day-to-day airport operations, safety, security and compliance
  • Managing and supporting an experienced airport operations team
  • Maintaining and reviewing the Aerodrome Manual, Transport Security Plan, Airport Emergency Plan and Safety Management System
  • Ensuring compliance with relevant CASA, Department of Home Affairs and other aviation regulatory requirements
  • Establishing effective systems for monitoring regulatory obligations and compliance milestones
  • Coordinating airport risk management, audits, emergency preparedness and compliance reporting
  • Liaising with regulators, airlines, airport tenants, contractors, emergency services and other stakeholders
  • Supporting airport projects, contracts, procurement and capital works
  • Contributing to airport master planning, aviation strategy, asset planning and operational improvement
  • Participating in the airport's on-call arrangements when required
  
The role combines genuine operational responsibility with leadership, governance and continuous improvement, providing the successful candidate with broad exposure across the airport function.

About You

You are an experienced airport operations professional who combines strong airside knowledge with sound judgement, organisation and people skills.

You may already be operating at a similar level within a regional airport, or you could be an experienced Airport Reporting Officer or senior airport operations professional ready to take the next step into a broader leadership position.

Council is not necessarily looking for someone who has spent years in management. More important is your practical airport knowledge, understanding of regulatory requirements and ability to work closely with an experienced operational team while providing the direction and accountability required.

You will bring:
  • Strong experience within airport operations, preferably with well-rounded airside exposure
  • Knowledge of aviation safety, security and regulatory compliance
  • An understanding of CASA requirements and the ability to interpret legislation, standards and regulatory instruments
  • Experience with airport operational manuals, procedures, safety systems or compliance documentation
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple regulatory requirements and deadlines
  • Leadership experience or demonstrated capability to step into a team leadership position
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • A practical, hands-on approach and willingness to work closely with the operational team
  • Airport Reporting Officer qualifications, or the ability to obtain these shortly after appointment
  • Air Radio Licence, or the ability to obtain one
  • Current driver's licence and ability to obtain an ASIC
  
Strong airside knowledge will be particularly valuable, including practical understanding of areas such as runway conditions, airfield lighting, wildlife management, vegetation, drainage and airside security requirements.

While ARO qualifications are preferred, Council is prepared to consider an exceptional candidate who brings the right broader aviation experience and can obtain the required qualifications shortly after appointment.

Why Join Fraser Coast Regional Council?

This opportunity offers:
  • A genuine 2IC opportunity working directly with the Airport Manager
  • The chance to take ownership of airport operations and compliance and make the role your own
  • Leadership of an experienced and well-established airport operations team
  • Broad exposure across airside operations, safety, security, compliance and airport projects
  • The opportunity to strengthen systems and influence how the airport operates into the future
  • Career progression for an experienced ARO or airport operations professional
  • A 9-day fortnight
  • Relocation assistance up to $6,000
  • The opportunity to live and work on Queensland's Fraser Coast
  
This is particularly well suited to someone currently working within a regional airport who is ready for greater responsibility, or an experienced professional from a larger airport looking for a broader role and a genuine coastal lifestyle change.

You'll join an Airport Manager who is looking for someone who can complement his experience, bring strong airside capability and work alongside him to continue developing the airport function. Most importantly, you'll have the freedom to establish systems, improve processes and take genuine ownership of the position.

Be part of a team responsible for keeping the Fraser Coast connected, while taking the next step in your aviation career.

Apply Now

To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:

Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au

Applications close: Tuesday 29 September 2026 at 5pm.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with customers, contractors and internal teams.

job.title: Housing Officer
job.description:
Housing Officer – Tenancy Services

Public Sector People is currently looking for an experienced Tenancy Manager to join an established community housing provider in Queensland.

This organisation provides secure and affordable housing to individuals and families across Queensland. Its approach combines effective tenancy management with early intervention, strong tenant relationships and connections to community support.

This is an opportunity to manage your own portfolio while helping tenants overcome challenges and maintain stable housing.

The Role

You will oversee the full tenancy lifecycle, from commencement and ongoing account management through to property care, complex tenancy matters and exits.

Rather than waiting for issues to escalate, you will work proactively with tenants to understand what is happening, identify practical solutions and connect them with appropriate support. You will balance empathy with accountability, ensuring tenancy obligations are understood and managed consistently.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing a portfolio of social and affordable housing tenancies
  • Establishing strong, professional relationships with tenants
  • Monitoring rent accounts and addressing arrears through early intervention
  • Coordinating tenancy commencements, reviews, transfers and exits
  • Responding to property care concerns, neighbourhood disputes and disruptive behaviour
  • Conducting tenant visits and property inspections where required
  • Developing repayment plans and sustainable tenancy strategies
  • Working with support providers, government agencies and internal property teams
  • Preparing notices, evidence and documentation for QCAT proceedings
  • Maintaining accurate case notes, records and tenancy documentation
  • Applying the Residential Tenancies and Rooming Accommodation Act 2008 and relevant organisational policies
About You

You will be comfortable managing competing priorities and making sound decisions in situations that are not always straightforward. You communicate clearly, remain calm during difficult conversations and understand how to combine good customer service with effective tenancy management.

You will ideally bring:
  • Experience in community housing, public housing, residential property management or a related service
  • Working knowledge of Queensland residential tenancy legislation
  • Experience managing arrears, tenancy breaches or complex customer matters
  • Strong negotiation, problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills
  • The confidence to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team
  • Accurate record-keeping and case management skills
  • A current Queensland Driver Licence
Experience working with people experiencing housing instability, financial hardship or other barriers would be highly regarded, as would previous involvement in QCAT matters.

What’s Available
  • Salary packaging benefits
  • SCHADS Award Level 4 conditions
  • Four days working onsite or across the portfolio, with one day from home
  • A supportive team environment with a strong community focus
  • The opportunity to contribute directly to housing stability across Queensland
If you are an experienced housing or property professional looking for a role with genuine social impact, we would be interested in hearing from you.

Apply now or contact Public Sector People for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Commissioning Technician

job.title: Development Engineer
job.description:
Development Engineer
Western Downs Regional Council | $107K–$114K + Super | 9-Day Fortnight
  
Looking for a Development Engineering role where you can do interesting technical work without sacrificing your work-life balance?
  
Public Sector People are partnering with Western Downs Regional Council to appoint a Development Engineer to join its planning and development function.
  
This is a broad, hands-on role where you’ll work across subdivisions, operational works, roads, stormwater, flooding and infrastructure planning while helping shape practical development outcomes across a growing regional community.
Importantly, this isn’t an environment where you’ll be buried under an unmanageable DA workload. You’ll join a supportive team with approximately 6–10 DAs per week across the team, alongside a 9-day fortnight and flexible working arrangements.
  
The Opportunity
  
Reporting to the Principal Planner, you’ll provide engineering input throughout the development assessment process, working closely with planners, developers, consultants, internal engineering teams and the wider community.
  
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Assessing development applications and Operational Works
  • Reviewing engineering designs and technical reports across stormwater, flooding and traffic
  • Providing practical engineering advice on subdivisions and development proposals
  • Undertaking site inspections and monitoring compliance with approvals and standards
  • Supporting pre-lodgement discussions with developers and consultants
  • Contributing to infrastructure planning, policy and LGIP matters
  • Working collaboratively to resolve technical issues and achieve sensible development outcomes
  
It’s a varied position where you’ll have the opportunity to influence projects from the early planning stages through to delivery.
  
About You
  
We’re looking for a practical and solutions-focused Civil Engineer who can balance good engineering with the realities of development, planning and stakeholder expectations.
  
You’ll ideally bring:
  • A Degree in Civil Engineering – mandatory
  • Development engineering experience across subdivisions and civil infrastructure
  • Knowledge of development assessment and relevant planning legislation
  • Ability to assess stormwater, flooding, traffic and broader civil engineering matters
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence working with developers, consultants and internal stakeholders
  • A collaborative and pragmatic approach to problem solving
  
RPEQ or progress towards RPEQ is highly regarded, as is previous experience within local government or a consultancy working with councils.
  
Why Western Downs?
  
This is an opportunity to step into a council offering the combination that can be difficult to find in Development Engineering: interesting work, autonomy, flexibility and a genuinely manageable workload.
  
You’ll benefit from a 9-day fortnight, flexible working arrangements and work-from-home options where practical, while working within a stable and supportive team.
  
For someone looking to move away from the pressures of a high-volume metropolitan DA environment—or an engineer wanting broader exposure and greater influence over development outcomes—this represents a strong long-term opportunity.
  
Apply
  
To apply for this role please attach a CV and cover letter using the ‘Apply Now’ function or for further information contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Consultant – Public Sector People
adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close: Friday 25th September at 4pm

job.title: Pre Construction Manager
job.description:
Pre-Construction Manager
Melbourne, VIC | Permanent Full-Time
 
The Opportunity
Design & Build Recruitment is partnering with a well-established and growing electrical services contractor to appoint an experienced Pre-Construction Manager.
This is a key leadership position sitting at the intersection of Estimating, Design and Operations, taking ownership of projects from early contractor involvement and tender stage through to procurement, delivery planning and operational handover.
 
The role will suit an experienced Project Manager, Senior Estimator, Pre-Construction Manager or Engineer who understands the realities of delivering complex construction projects and enjoys influencing outcomes before construction begins.
With a strong pipeline of major projects and continued business growth, this position offers the opportunity to establish and develop a dedicated pre-construction function, with the expectation that the successful candidate will eventually lead a team.
 
The Role
As Pre-Construction Manager, you will play a critical role in ensuring projects transition effectively from concept and tender through to delivery.
Working closely with senior leadership, estimators, designers and project delivery teams, you will lead ECI and bid opportunities, review major project estimates, identify commercial and technical risks, and develop operational budgets and production metrics ahead of project commencement.
You will remain involved through early design and procurement, ensuring a structured and commercially robust handover into operations.
 
Key Responsibilities
Tender & Estimating
  • Lead and coordinate ECI and major bid opportunities alongside estimating and design teams.
  • Review significant project estimates through to final negotiation stages.
  • Provide input into buildability, constructability and design reviews.
  • Support labour rate build-ups, schedules of rates and standardised estimating information.
  • Provide technical and commercial advice around client budgets, design and project strategy.
  • Support business development activity and major tender opportunities.
Pre-Construction & Project Planning
  • Translate awarded project estimates into operational budgets and production metrics.
  • Undertake detailed reviews of project scope, design and documentation ahead of delivery.
  • Establish and manage project Risk & Opportunity registers.
  • Identify value engineering and design efficiency opportunities.
  • Coordinate early procurement of long-lead and engineered equipment.
  • Lead formal project handovers from pre-construction into operational delivery teams.
  • Coordinate early design engagement with clients and internal design teams.
Project Delivery Support
  • Maintain involvement through early design and procurement stages.
  • Support project teams during the transition into construction.
  • Drive lessons learned and continuous improvement across project delivery.
Leadership & Process Improvement
  • Improve pre-construction processes, systems, templates and reporting.
  • Maintain accurate records across estimates, budgets and handover documentation.
  • Provide reporting on pipeline opportunities, project handovers and key lessons learned.
  • Play a key role in developing the future pre-construction function, with the opportunity to build and lead a team.
About You
We are looking for someone with a strong understanding of the construction lifecycle and the ability to bridge the gap between winning work and successfully delivering it.
You may currently be working as a:
  • Pre-Construction Manager
  • Senior Project Manager
  • Project Manager with strong estimating experience
  • Senior Estimator looking to move closer to project strategy and delivery
  • Electrical or Building Services Engineer with significant commercial project experience
Ideally, you will bring:
  • Experience in project management and/or engineering combined with estimating experience within the construction industry.
  • A strong understanding of buildability, constructability and design review.
  • Experience across the full project lifecycle, from ECI and tender through to design, procurement and project handover.
  • The ability to review complex scopes and identify commercial, technical and delivery risks.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to work across estimating, design, operations and client teams.
  • Experience identifying value engineering and design efficiency opportunities.
  • Excellent analytical, commercial and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Experience within electrical services, building services, industrial construction, infrastructure or mission-critical/data centre environments will be highly regarded.
 
What's On Offer?
This is a genuine opportunity to take ownership of a critical function within a growing contractor.
You will have:
  • A highly influential role across major projects.
  • Package: $180,000 - $220,000 + super + vehicle/car allowance (DOE)
  • Exposure to projects from tender through to delivery.
  • The opportunity to shape and improve pre-construction processes.
  • Close collaboration with senior leadership.
  • A clear pathway into building and leading a dedicated pre-construction team.
  • A strong pipeline of complex electrical and infrastructure projects.
  • A permanent, long-term career opportunity with a growing Melbourne-based contractor.
Apply
If you are an experienced construction professional looking to move into a strategic pre-construction leadership role, we'd like to hear from you.
For a confidential discussion, please contact Connor Gwilliam at Design & Build Recruitment, or apply directly via the link below.
All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

job.title: Water & Wastewater Treatment Engineer
job.description:
Water & Wastewater Treatment Engineer
Cowra Council
Cowra, NSW

$114,359 - $128,712 + super | 35-hour week | Nine-day fortnight

Cowra Council is seeking a Water & Wastewater Treatment Engineer to provide engineering leadership across its water and sewage treatment operations.

This is an opportunity to oversee five treatment facilities, improve operational performance and quality systems, and help Council modernise the way it manages critical water infrastructure.

Reporting to the Manager - Cowra Works, you'll lead through an experienced Supervisor and ganger, supporting a qualified team of operators with substantial site and process knowledge.

Council is seeking strong engineering thinking and relevant treatment experience. Civil and chemical engineers are particularly well aligned, although candidates from other relevant engineering disciplines with substantial water or wastewater treatment experience will also be considered.

The Opportunity
This role combines treatment-process engineering, operational leadership, quality control and continuous improvement.

Working across three water treatment plants and two sewage treatment plants, you'll oversee treatment performance, testing, monitoring, optimisation, source-water protection and associated mechanical, electrical, instrumentation and telemetry systems.

The portfolio offers exposure to modern membrane filtration alongside traditional treatment methods, as well as input into plant refurbishment and asset-renewal projects.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the operation, maintenance, monitoring and optimisation of Council's water and sewage treatment facilities.
  • Provide direction and technical support to the Supervisor, ganger and operational team.
  • Maintain treatment quality, environmental and Drinking Water Management systems.
  • Ensure compliance with legislation, standards, licence conditions and external audit requirements.
  • Oversee mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, telemetry and process-control systems.
  • Manage operational reporting, assigned budgets, emergency work and contractor services.
  • Provide treatment expertise to asset-renewal, refurbishment and improvement projects.
  • Drive continuous improvement in process performance, safety, quality and system maturity.
About You
This role would suit a Water Treatment Engineer, Wastewater Treatment Engineer, Process Engineer, Chemical Engineer or Civil Engineer with relevant treatment-operations experience.

You will be technically credible, comfortable working alongside experienced operators and able to investigate issues, develop recommendations and bring well-considered information forward for decision.

You will bring:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Chemical Engineering or another relevant engineering discipline.
  • Relevant experience across water treatment, wastewater treatment or comparable process operations.
  • Knowledge of treatment optimisation, quality control and operational compliance.
  • Sound judgement and the ability to work with a high degree of autonomy.
  • Experience leading operators, supervisors, contractors or multidisciplinary technical teams.
  • Strong communication, reporting and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Current Class C Driver Licence.
Government experience is preferred, although candidates from utilities, consultancies, contractors and other regulated process environments are encouraged to apply.

Why Cowra?
Cowra Council offers broad technical exposure that can be difficult to gain in a larger organisation: five treatment facilities, varied treatment methodologies and the ability to see the direct community impact of your work.

You'll join a capable and well-regarded operational team, with experienced leaders and qualified operators who can provide strong local knowledge. Council also maintains supportive relationships with NSW Public Works and NSW Health.

Cowra provides an affordable regional lifestyle, strong schooling and community facilities, with Orange, Bathurst and Young within reach. The role offers meaningful responsibility, work-life balance and room to continue developing your technical and leadership career.

Benefits
  • Salary of $114,359 - $128,712 plus super.
  • Permanent full-time position.
  • 35-hour working week with a nine-day fortnight.
  • Relocation assistance covering up to two-thirds of eligible relocation costs.
  • Professional development and access to external technical support.
  • Exposure to five treatment facilities and varied treatment technologies.
  • Affordable regional lifestyle with visible community impact.
How to Apply
Public Sector People is managing this recruitment process on behalf of Cowra Council.

For a confidential discussion, please contact:
Will Cooke
Senior Consultant - Public Sector People
0412 950 548
wcooke@publicsectorpeople.com.au

job.title: Manager (Infrastructure & Strategic Planning)
job.description:
This QLD state department is seeking an experienced Traffic and Transport Engineer / Infrastructure Planning professional to join their team supporting major development and infrastructure initiatives.
  
This is a senior technical and strategic role suited to someone with strong experience across traffic and transport engineering, development assessment, infrastructure planning and stakeholder engagement.
  
You will provide authoritative, practical advice to support timely development approvals, integrated transport outcomes and sustainable development, applying sound engineering judgement while balancing development objectives, infrastructure requirements and regulatory standards.
  
Key Responsibilities
  • Provide expert traffic and transport advice to develop integrated transport infrastructure strategies for Priority Development Areas (PDAs), including infrastructure planning and infrastructure charges.
  • Provide technical input throughout the development assessment process, including reviewing complex proposals and negotiating appropriate traffic, transport and infrastructure outcomes.
  • Provide strategic advice across transport planning, traffic modelling, infrastructure strategy and development planning.
  • Integrate land use, transport and infrastructure requirements to support coordinated and sustainable development outcomes.
  • Identify risks, opportunities and practical solutions across complex traffic, transport and infrastructure matters.
  • Translate complex technical issues into clear, practical and defensible recommendations to support timely decision-making.
  • Build strong relationships with government agencies, infrastructure authorities, developers, consultants and industry stakeholders.
  • Lead stakeholder discussions and negotiations to resolve complex infrastructure issues and achieve practical outcomes.
  • Maintain quality assurance and consistency across traffic and transport advice.
  • Manage multiple priorities and complex workstreams with a high level of autonomy.
  
About You
We are looking for an experienced traffic and transport engineering professional who can combine technical expertise with strategic thinking and development assessment capability.
  
You will bring:
  • Comprehensive knowledge of contemporary transport planning and design principles, standards, legislation and related disciplines.
  • Significant experience in integrated transport planning, infrastructure strategy, transport infrastructure and development assessment.
  • Strong experience assessing complex development proposals and providing technical advice that supports development outcomes.
  • Demonstrated leadership capability and strong professional judgement.
  • Advanced stakeholder management and negotiation skills, particularly across complex or competing infrastructure requirements.
  • The ability to develop pragmatic and innovative solutions within a dynamic development and policy environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical matters clearly and persuasively.
  • Strong project and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outcomes with limited supervision.
  • Previous experience within Queensland Government, Economic Development Queensland (EDQ), major development or large infrastructure environments will be highly regarded.
  
The Opportunity
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Traffic/Transport Engineer or Infrastructure Planning professional to influence major development and infrastructure outcomes within Queensland Government.
  
The successful candidate will be more than a technical reviewer — you will be expected to lead complex traffic and transport matters, exercise sound professional judgement, negotiate practical outcomes and provide clear advice that directly supports development and infrastructure decision-making.
