job.title: Water & Wastewater Network Engineer
job.description:
Water & Wastewater Network Engineer
Cowra Council | Cowra, NSW

$114,359–$128,712 + super | 35-hour week | Nine-day fortnight

Cowra Council is seeking a Water & Wastewater Network Engineer to lead its water and wastewater reticulation services.

This is a broad technical leadership role spanning network operations, asset planning, customer service, development assessment and the delivery of renewal and improvement works.

Reporting to the Manager - Cowra Works, you'll provide leadership through an experienced Supervisor and two gangers, supporting a wider team of eight water and wastewater attendants.

Council is open to qualified engineers and experienced water-sector professionals with strong practical knowledge of reticulation systems. Local Government experience is valued, but relevant experience from utilities, contractors and other technical environments will also be considered.

The Opportunity
This role combines operational leadership, network engineering and long-term infrastructure planning across Cowra’s water and sewer reticulation systems.

You'll oversee reticulation operations, support responses to faults and customer issues, assess water and wastewater components of development applications, and contribute to renewal programs including water main replacement and wastewater relining.

With a significant residential subdivision under assessment and continued regional growth, you'll also help Council understand network capacity, plan future upgrades and maintain reliable services for the community.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the operation and maintenance of Council's water and wastewater reticulation systems.
  • Provide direction and support to the Supervisor, gangers and operational team.
  • Support network modelling, capacity assessments and planning for future upgrades.
  • Assess developers' civil plans and drawings against relevant standards and Council policies.
  • Help develop and deliver asset renewal programs, including water main replacement and wastewater relining.
  • Oversee customer enquiries, emergency work and unscheduled network issues.
  • Contribute to tenders, contractor management, strategic planning and asset management activities.
  • Drive continuous improvement in service quality, safety, performance and customer outcomes.
About You
This role would suit a Civil or Water Engineer, network specialist, Senior Technical Officer or experienced water operations professional ready to take broader responsibility for an essential community service.

You may already be working in Local Government or a utility, or bring transferable experience from a contractor, consultancy or technical operations environment.

You will bring:
  • Tertiary qualifications in engineering or a relevant technical discipline, or substantial practical water and wastewater experience.
  • Strong knowledge of water and wastewater reticulation, pumping and network operations.
  • Sound judgement and the ability to resolve operational and technical problems autonomously.
  • Experience leading operational staff, supervisors, contractors or multidisciplinary teams.
  • Strong communication skills and confidence working with residents, developers and internal stakeholders.
  • Understanding of asset planning, renewals, relevant standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Current Class C Driver Licence.
Experience within Local Government and exposure to development assessment or network modelling will be advantageous.

Why Cowra?
Cowra Council offers the opportunity to work closely with the community and see the direct impact of your decisions across an essential public service.

You'll inherit an experienced and committed operational team with strong local knowledge, while working alongside internal project, asset and technical specialists and receiving support from organisations including NSW Public Works.

Cowra provides an affordable regional lifestyle, strong schooling and community facilities, with Orange, Bathurst and Young within reach. It is well suited to professionals seeking greater responsibility, work-life balance and the opportunity to build a life in regional NSW.

Benefits
  • Salary of $114,359 - $128,712 plus super.
  • Permanent full-time position.
  • 35-hour working week with a nine-day fortnight.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance Technician — Sterile Injectables

Location: Chatswood, NSW
Industry: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing (Sterile Injectables)
Hours: Monday–Friday, 8am–4pm (training period), transitioning to rotating 8am–4pm / 7am–3pm shifts
Salary: $100,000–$115,000 + phone + discretionary bonus

 About the Company

Our client is an Australian-owned pharmaceutical manufacturer supplying hospitals nationally and exporting to international markets, with active plans for further global expansion. While smaller than the multinational giants, the business offers genuine access to senior leadership — including regular contact with the CEO — and continued investment in new machinery and cleanroom infrastructure.

This is a business with a strong retention track record: the maintenance team has very low turnover, with tenures ranging from 3 to 20+ years. You'll be joining a close-knit, growing team of 4.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on Maintenance Technician to join the site's maintenance team, working across cleanroom and aseptic suite environments supporting liquid filling and sterile injectable manufacturing. This is a step up for someone with tablet/solid-dose maintenance experience looking to move into liquid/sterile processing — or a great fit for someone already working in sterile injectables.

You'll partner closely with a senior technician during onboarding before moving onto the standard rotating roster.

Reporting to: Asset Manager (who reports to the Chief Operations Manager, then CEO)

Key Responsibilities

- Perform preventative maintenance on equipment, critical systems, and services — including purified water systems, cleanroom/aseptic suite systems, vision systems, blister and packaging equipment, and vial-based theatre pack lines (vials sterilised for direct use in operating theatres)
- Attend to breakdowns and troubleshoot faults across equipment, critical systems, and services, escalating to external contractors when a fault is beyond in-house scope
- Investigate and report breakdown root causes and concerns to management
- Ensure adherence to the preventative maintenance schedule
- Document all work and maintain accurate records in the CMMS within a cGMP-compliant change control environment
- Coordinate maintenance and repair activities with external service providers as required

What You'll Also Do

- Follow standard operating procedures in all work performed
- Complete GMP-standard documentation for work activities
- Contribute to the development of procedures and related documentation
- Support investigations into incidents, accidents, quality, and governance issues as needed
- Work collaboratively across Production, R&D, NPI, Validation, and QA/QC to support business objectives
- Identify, assess, and control workplace hazards and risks
- Report any accidents or incidents on the day they occur

 About You

- Mechanically minded, with proven maintenance technician experience in a regulated pharmaceutical environment
- Liquid filling / sterile injectable manufacturing experience strongly preferred; solid dose (tablet) experience will also be considered
- Food manufacturing background is not a fit for this role
- Working knowledge of CMMS platforms
- Exposure to equipment commissioning and validation processes
- Strong troubleshooting and fault-finding skills across mechanical, electrical, or utilities systems (purified water systems, vision systems, packaging lines)
- Comfortable working to GMP/cGMP standards and change control processes
- A collaborative approach and willingness to train and support colleagues
- Strong commitment to workplace health and safety
- No formal pharma qualification required — full training and support provided; the business will also consider candidates straight out of a mechanical apprenticeship


 Why Apply

- Direct, regular exposure to senior leadership including the CEO — a level of access not typical at larger multinational manufacturers
- Genuinely low staff turnover and a stable, tenured team culture
- Ongoing investment in new equipment and cleanroom upgrades
- Structured onboarding alongside a senior technician
- Company-supported training courses (up to $2,000) and career development, including pathways for apprentice-level candidates
- A growing, internationally expanding business with export markets beyond Australia

Interested in learning more? Apply now or reach out for a confidential conversation.

  • Excellent stakeholder management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects across different states.
Benefits & Perks
  • $170,000 + Super

  • Opportunity to work on the rapidly growing C&I battery storage market
  • Exposure to technically complex BESS and renewable energy projects
  • High level of ownership and autonomy across the project portfolio

Apply Today

  • Landmark and technically challenging projects.

job.title: Structural Engineer
job.description:
Structural Engineer

Looking for a Civil/Structural Engineer for a well-established, niche Consulting Engineering and Building Design firm based in Southern Sydney, with a strong focus on structural engineering.

Our work is predominantly centred around the assessment, investigation and design of existing residential structures, including buildings impacted by fire, tree and vehicle damage, as well as structural defects and remedial works.

We are seeking a motivated and detail-driven Civil/Structural Engineer to join our growing team. This is a great opportunity for an engineer who enjoys structural engineering, wants strong technical exposure and is keen to develop their career alongside experienced senior engineers.

The role is highly structures-focused, with exposure to structural assessment, site investigations, causation reporting, remedial design and structural design across timber, steel and concrete.

Key Responsibilities
  • Undertake structural inspections and assessments of existing buildings.
  • Investigate structural defects, damage and failures and determine causation.
  • Prepare detailed technical and causation reports.
  • Develop scopes of structural and remedial works.
  • Undertake structural analysis and design across timber, steel and concrete.
  • Prepare structural drawings and documentation using AutoCAD.
  • Liaise with clients, contractors and other stakeholders.
  • Work closely with senior engineers and contribute to project delivery.
Skills & Experience
  • Civil or Structural Engineering degree.
  • Experience in structural consulting or building design is desirable.
  • Strong understanding of structural behaviour and engineering fundamentals.
  • Developing or demonstrated capability in timber, steel and concrete design.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent technical report writing and written English.
  • High attention to detail.
  • Proficiency in AutoCAD.
  • Strong communication skills and a willingness to attend site.
  • Genuine interest in developing a career in structural engineering.
Why Join us?
  • Structures-heavy workload with genuine technical exposure.
  • Work across investigation, assessment, remedial and new structural design.
  • Mentoring from experienced senior engineers.
  • 30-week Engineering Seminar Program.
  • Exposure to a broad range of structures across NSW and ACT.
  • Competitive remuneration and performance-based bonuses.
  • Company vehicle provided as part of the remuneration package.
  • Long-term career opportunity within a growing specialist consultancy

job.title: General Foreman
job.description:
The Company

A highly regarded, privately owned Sydney builder with an exceptional track record delivering large-scale residential and mixed-use developments.

Known for their strong systems, experienced project teams and consistently high standards of delivery, they have established long-term relationships with some of Australia's leading developers. Their continued success has created a significant pipeline of major residential projects across Sydney.

Just as importantly, this is a business that invests heavily in its people, providing genuine career development and opportunities to progress through the site management ranks.

The Opportunity

An outstanding opportunity exists for an experienced General Foreman to take a key leadership position on a major $190M apartment development in Sydney's Inner West.

Working alongside an experienced Site Manager and Project Manager, you'll be responsible for driving day-to-day construction activity across a large, fast-moving residential project.

This is a genuine senior site role with the scale, resources and project team around you to deliver successfully — ideal for a proven General Foreman who enjoys taking ownership and driving performance on major builds.

The Role

Reporting to the Site Manager, you will be responsible for:
  • Leading daily construction activities and subcontractor coordination
  • Managing Foremen, Leading Hands and trades across multiple work fronts
  • Driving short-term programming, sequencing and site productivity
  • Coordinating structure, façade, services and finishes packages
  • Maintaining strict QA standards throughout construction
  • Managing site logistics and ensuring works remain ahead of program
  • Leading toolbox talks and maintaining a strong safety-first culture
  • Working closely with the project team to resolve design and buildability issues
  • Driving the project through key milestones and ultimately towards successful completion
About You
  • Trade-qualified, ideally with a carpentry background
  • Proven experience as a General Foreman or Senior Foreman on major apartment developments
  • Strong background delivering large-scale Class 2 residential projects
  • Excellent understanding of structure, façade, services and finishes
  • Proven ability to coordinate large subcontractor teams and multiple work fronts
  • Strong programming and sequencing capability
  • A confident leader who can drive performance while maintaining a positive site culture
In Return
  • Salary package up to $260,000, depending on experience
  • Take a senior site leadership role on a major Inner West apartment development
  • Join one of Sydney's most established large-scale residential builders
  • Work alongside an experienced and well-resourced project team
  • Strong pipeline of major residential projects offering long-term security
  • Genuine progression opportunities towards Site Manager and Senior Site Manager
  • A business with a proven track record of developing and promoting its people internally
How to Apply Click Apply and include your CV and project list (Word format preferred).

For a confidential discussion about this opportunity, contact Mitchell Barker on 0423 927 536.

All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality.

Lead the development of data governance and privacy frameworks that shape how information is managed across government, using your expertise in governance, stakeholder engagement and privacy impact assessments to deliver practical, high-quality outcomes.

What's involved:
  
This is a delivery-focused specialist role that will help strengthen the approach to data governance, open data and privacy management while building organisational capability and supporting trusted information practices.
  
The Senior Data Governance & Privacy Specialist will undertake activities including:
  
Leading the development of data and open data governance frameworks, policies, procedures and associated artefacts.
• Developing governance standards, controls, templates, accountability models, guidance materials and supporting documentation.
• Partnering with information owners, system owners and subject matter experts to understand information assets and business requirements.
• Completing Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), including privacy risk identification, treatment actions and practical recommendations.
• Supporting compliance with Queensland Government legislation, directives and policies including information privacy, information security and open data requirements.
• Preparing executive briefings, decision papers, status reports and recommendations for senior leaders and governance forums.
• Managing multiple workstreams while providing updates on risks, dependencies and delivery progress.
• Developing practical knowledge content, templates and handover materials to support ongoing capability uplift across the organisation.
  
  
About you:
  
  • Available to commence as soon as possible.
  • Demonstrated experience developing data governance and open data governance frameworks, policies, procedures and supporting governance materials.
  • Strong experience conducting Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and documenting privacy risk treatment strategies.
  • Sound understanding of information governance, data management, records management, risk and assurance principles.
  • Previous Queensland Government or public sector experience is highly regarded.
  • Excellent written communication skills with experience preparing executive briefs, governance artefacts and guidance materials.

job.title: Contract Administrator - Multi-Storey Commercial Construction Melbourne West
job.description:
Truganina | Permanent
The Opportunity
A growing Melbourne-based commercial and industrial builder is looking to appoint two Contract Administrators to support the delivery of new multi-storey projects in Melbourne's western suburbs, with the immediate focus being Truganina.

The business has recently secured a five-storey mixed-use development as part of a broader five-building masterplan. There is also potential for an additional adjacent project of a similar scope.

This represents an exciting period of growth for the business as it continues to expand its capabilities beyond its traditional industrial portfolio and into more complex multi-storey commercial and mixed-use construction.

About the Business
The company is an established Victorian construction and development business with a strong track record across:
  • Industrial and logistics
  • Warehousing and distribution
  • Commercial
  • Office
  • Retail
  • Hospitality
  • Mixed-use developments
They have built their reputation around quality construction, strong client relationships and a hands-on approach to project delivery.
The business has a collaborative and practical culture, with a strong emphasis on teamwork, accountability and delivering quality outcomes rather than operating within a heavily corporate environment.

Why This Role Is Different
The business has traditionally delivered a significant volume of industrial construction, where projects can be relatively straightforward from a commercial and contractual perspective.

The new multi-storey projects introduce a different level of complexity, including:
  • Multiple levels and building interfaces
  • Greater design development
  • Increased consultant coordination
  • More complex subcontractor packages
  • Significant variation and change management
  • More involved services coordination
  • Greater client and consultant interaction
  • Design changes throughout construction
  • Increased commercial and programme implications
As a result, they are specifically looking for CAs who understand how to manage the commercial consequences of change, rather than simply administering straightforward subcontract packages.

The Role
Working closely with the Project Manager and site team, you will take responsibility for the commercial and contractual administration of your project.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing subcontractor packages from procurement through to completion
  • Preparing and administering subcontracts and purchase orders
  • Reviewing subcontractor scopes and quotations
  • Managing progress claims and payment schedules
  • Assessing, negotiating and administering variations
  • Managing EOTs and contractual notices
  • Identifying the commercial impact of design and scope changes
  • Maintaining accurate cost reporting and forecasting
  • Managing RFIs and coordinating with consultants and subcontractors
  • Reviewing drawings, specifications and design changes
  • Supporting procurement and subcontractor negotiations
  • Maintaining project registers and commercial documentation
  • Working closely with the PM to maintain project budgets and programme
  • Supporting the project through to final account and handover
What We're Looking For The ideal candidate will have:
  • 4+ years' experience as a Contract Administrator
  • Strong commercial construction experience
  • Experience across multi-storey commercial, residential or mixed-use projects
  • Strong understanding of variations, EOTs, progress claims and subcontract administration
  • Experience managing design and scope changes
  • Strong procurement and subcontractor management skills
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings and specifications
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Strong commercial awareness and attention to detail
  • A proactive approach to identifying and resolving issues
If you're a CA looking to broaden your experience into more complex multi-storey construction and want to join a growing builder where you can have genuine ownership of your projects, this could be an excellent next step

job.title: Civil Works Manager
job.description:
Civil Works Manager
North Burnett Regional Council | Mundubbera, QLD | Civil Works & Infrastructure | Circa $150K base + Accommodation + Car allowance
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with North Burnett Regional Council to recruit an experienced Civil Works Manager to provide strategic and operational leadership across Council's civil works and open spaces functions. This is an outstanding opportunity for a hands-on, visible and people-focused leader who wants to make a genuine difference.
  
This position suits a pro-active leader who will get out across the region, spend time with their teams, understand the condition of the network, visit works in progress and actively resolve the issues that impact employees and the community.
  
With teams operating across six townships, visibility matters. The successful candidate will be expected to build strong relationships with staff, provide clear direction and create an environment where people feel supported, developed and accountable.
  
The Role
  
Reporting to the General Manager Works, you will lead the delivery of Council's civil works services across a diverse regional portfolio encompassing rural and urban roads, bridges, parks and open spaces, aerodromes and cemeteries.
There is a significant opportunity to make your mark.
  
Council is rebuilding momentum across its civil works program, with a strong focus on road renewals, resheeting, resealing and bridge repairs. You'll inherit capable people within the team, while having the opportunity to strengthen leadership, develop emerging talent and improve how works are planned, prioritised and delivered.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  
  • Providing visible, hands-on leadership across geographically dispersed civil works and open spaces teams
  • Leading, coaching and developing staff while building accountability, capability and succession
  • Overseeing the delivery and maintenance of Council's rural and urban road networks and associated infrastructure
  • Developing maintenance programs and identifying renewal priorities through sound asset management practices
  • Leading the planning and delivery of Council's civil capital works program
  • Managing operational and capital budgets and ensuring resources are directed to the areas of greatest need
  • Driving improvements in productivity, plant utilisation, safety and service delivery
  • Working closely with contractors, consultants and internal teams to achieve value-for-money outcomes
  • Building trusted relationships with stakeholders and communities across the North Burnett region
  • Providing clear, consistent and evidence-based advice while following issues through to resolution.
  
The formal position description reinforces this emphasis on visible leadership, staff capability, accountability and safety alongside asset management and capital delivery.
  
About You
  
You are an experienced civil works or infrastructure professional, but importantly, you are a leader who enjoys being involved.
  
You'll be comfortable walking into a depot and talking with frontline employees, visiting a road or project to understand an issue firsthand, mentoring an engineer who wants to progress their career, and then presenting clear and credible advice to senior leadership or elected members.
  
You will bring:
  • Strong experience across civil works, roads, infrastructure maintenance or construction
  • Proven experience leading operational and geographically dispersed teams
  • A hands-on and highly visible leadership style
  • A genuine commitment to coaching, mentoring and developing people
  • Strong asset management and capital works planning capability
  • Sound commercial, financial and project management experience
  • A practical understanding of safety within civil construction and maintenance environments
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to engage equally well with frontline staff, technical professionals, executives and elected members
  • Energy, initiative and a willingness to challenge existing ways of working and implement improvements
  • High levels of integrity, accountability and follow-through.
  
Council is open-minded regarding where you have developed your experience. You may already be working within local or state government, or you may come from civil construction, consulting or another infrastructure environment and be looking to bring your experience into a broader community-focused leadership role. The client specifically confirmed that local government experience is not essential and is interested in candidates who bring energy, ideas and the ability to implement change.
  
A Civil Engineering background and RPEQ would be highly regarded although this is not essential. More important is having the technical credibility to be an informed client and provide sound leadership across the function.
  
Why Join North Burnett Regional Council?
  
This is a role where you can see the impact of your leadership.
  
You'll have the opportunity to strengthen an established team, develop future leaders, rebuild momentum across the road network and introduce new ideas that improve how Council delivers services to its communities. Council sees a genuine opportunity for innovation and more cost-effective delivery as it continues a multi-year program of rebuilding its road network.
  
The package includes:
  • Circa $150,000 base salary
  • $25,000 vehicle allowance
  • Remote locality allowance
  • $5,000 professional development allowance
  • Five weeks annual leave plus leave loading
  • Relocation assistance for the successful candidate
  • Access to Council housing in Mundubbera
  
If you're a civil infrastructure professional who believes leadership means being present, developing your people, communicating clearly and taking ownership of outcomes, this is an opportunity to have a genuine impact across an entire region.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Sunday 20th September at 4pm

job.title: Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead
job.description:
Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead
Noosa Council | Noosa, QLD | $109,838 Base | $124,675 TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Noosa Council to recruit an experienced Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead.
  
This is much more than a business-as-usual taxation position.
It is a senior specialist opportunity to lead Council’s response to two critical taxation compliance projects relating to Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee.
  
Reporting to the Financial Services Manager, you will combine advanced technical taxation knowledge with strong project delivery capability. You will identify and quantify areas of exposure, lead remediation activities and embed governance frameworks that support sustainable compliance beyond the life of the projects.
The role will also provide specialist advice across Goods and Services Tax, contractor classification, supplier taxation obligations and other associated compliance risks.
  
Council needs someone who can do more than identify problems. You will need to translate complex legislation into practical solutions, bring clarity to accountabilities and deliver lasting improvements across finance, payroll, human resources, procurement and governance.
  
The Opportunity
This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports. Your influence will come through your technical expertise, judgement, stakeholder capability and ability to lead complex work through to completion.
You will take ownership of the end-to-end delivery of Council’s priority taxation compliance projects, ensuring milestones, deliverables and outcomes are achieved within agreed timeframes.
  
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading specialist compliance projects relating to Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee
  • Acting as Council’s taxation and compliance specialist within Financial Services
  • Providing expert advice across FBT, GST, Superannuation Guarantee, contractor classification and supplier-related taxation obligations
  • Undertaking retrospective compliance reviews, including data analysis, risk identification and impact assessment
  • Quantifying potential exposure and developing practical remediation strategies
  • Designing and embedding fit-for-purpose governance frameworks, policies, procedures and internal controls
  • Partnering with Finance, Remuneration and Benefits, Human Resources, Procurement and Governance teams
  • Clarifying responsibilities and supporting informed decision-making across multidisciplinary teams
  • Managing engagement with external taxation advisers and specialists, ensuring quality, value for money and timely delivery
  • Preparing executive-level briefings, risk assessments, options papers and recommendations
  • Managing project scope, dependencies, milestones and progress reporting
  • Building organisational capability through structured knowledge transfer, clear documentation and practical guidance
  • Ensuring responsibility for ongoing compliance can transition effectively into operational teams at the completion of the projects
  
About You
You will be an experienced taxation, superannuation or compliance professional who is comfortable taking ownership of complex and potentially sensitive issues.
  
You will bring strong technical knowledge, but equally important will be your ability to apply that knowledge in a practical organisational environment. You will know how to move from identifying an issue to quantifying the risk, recommending a course of action and implementing a sustainable solution.
  
You’ll bring:
  • Demonstrated experience leading taxation, superannuation or compliance-focused projects within a large or complex organisation
  • Advanced knowledge of Australian taxation legislation relating to payroll and employment arrangements
  • Strong technical capability across Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee
  • Knowledge of GST, contractor engagement models and supplier-related taxation obligations
  • Proven experience conducting retrospective compliance reviews and identifying regulatory risk
  • Experience supporting taxation remediation and broader governance improvement initiatives
  • Strong project governance and delivery capability, including managing scope, dependencies, milestones and reporting
  • Experience designing and implementing policies, procedures and internal control frameworks
  • Highly developed stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • The ability to translate complex legislative and technical requirements into clear, practical advice
  • Strong written capability, including the preparation of executive briefings, risk assessments and recommendations
  • The confidence to work across multidisciplinary teams while maintaining clear advisory and operational accountabilities
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and the judgement to work through competing risks and priorities
  
You will also hold:
  • A degree in accounting, finance, business or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrated knowledge and experience in taxation, financial compliance and governance
  • A current C Class driver licence
  
Membership of, or progress towards membership of, a recognised professional accounting body would be advantageous.
  
Previous experience within local government or the broader public sector would be highly regarded but is not essential. Council will also consider candidates from complex corporate environments who can demonstrate the required taxation expertise, governance awareness and project delivery capability.
  
Why Noosa Council?
  
At Noosa Council, being “Different by Nature” reflects more than the region’s location. It represents how Council supports its people, serves its community and protects one of Australia’s most distinctive natural environments.
Based on Kabi Kabi Country, Noosa Shire is home to more than 56,000 residents and covers 872 square kilometres. Internationally recognised as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the region offers an exceptional combination of beaches, national parks, lakes and hinterland communities.
Council employs more than 500 people and plays an important role in delivering a sustainable future for the shire.
  
This opportunity offers:
  
  • Full-time, fixed-term employment through to 30 June 2027
  • LGOA Level 6 base salary of $109,838
  • Total remuneration package of $124,675, inclusive of 12% employer superannuation and 17.5% leave loading
  • Applicable salary increases under Council’s Certified Agreement 2025
  • Flexible working arrangements 
  • Five days of Wellbeing Leave
  • Five days of Reproductive Health Leave
  • Employee Assistance Program and workplace wellbeing initiatives
  • Training, mentoring and professional development opportunities
  • The opportunity to deliver meaningful improvements that will strengthen Council’s financial governance and compliance environment
  
This is an opportunity to work where others holiday while delivering complex, high-value work that will have a lasting organisational impact.
  
If you are an experienced taxation or compliance professional looking for an opportunity where you can solve complex problems, lead critical projects and build a stronger governance environment, we would like to hear from you.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the “Apply Now” button or contact:
Paul Johanson
QLD State Manager
Public Sector People
E: pjohanson@publicsectorpeople.com.au
M: 0401 857 515
www.publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Friday 18 September 2026.
  
Appointment will be subject to Noosa Council’s required pre-employment checks.

job.title: Manager Communities & Cultural Services
job.description:
Manager Community & Cultural Services
Central Highlands Regional Council | Emerald, QLD | $210K–$252K TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Central Highlands Regional Council to recruit an experienced and progressive Manager Community & Cultural Services.
  
This is much more than a traditional community services role.
  
It is an opportunity for an accomplished leader to take responsibility for a broad, highly visible portfolio of services that directly influence the lives of communities across the Central Highlands – and to help shape what those services look like into the future.
  
Council is looking for someone who enjoys solving problems, developing people and bringing structure to a diverse service portfolio. You won't be expected to arrive with every answer, but you will need the leadership capability, judgement and curiosity to find them.
  
With important foundations already being put in place, the incoming Manager will have a genuine opportunity to build momentum, strengthen governance and team capability, and put their own stamp on the future direction of the function.
  
The Opportunity
  
Reporting to the Director Communities, you will lead a diverse portfolio encompassing arts and culture, community grants, community relationships, youth, reconciliation, libraries, regional events and human and social recovery.
  
The breadth of the portfolio is what makes this opportunity different. Council isn't looking for a specialist who has spent their career focused exclusively on one element of community or cultural services. They need a leader who can see the bigger picture, bring different functions together and ensure people, resources and services are aligned with Council and community priorities.
  
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Providing strategic and operational leadership across Council's Community and Cultural Services portfolio
  • Leading, coaching and developing a diverse team, strengthening capability, accountability and performance
  • Driving the delivery and continuous improvement of community-facing programs and services
  • Leading the development and implementation of key strategies across libraries, arts, culture and heritage
  • Progressing Council's Community Grants Program and ensuring strong governance and alignment with community priorities
  • Managing budgets and resources while ensuring services demonstrate value and financial accountability
  • Building productive relationships with community organisations, government agencies, funding bodies, Traditional Owners and regional partners
  • Working closely with Councillors and SLT in providing clear, considered and evidence-based advice
  • Strengthening governance, systems and processes across the portfolio
  • Identifying opportunities to innovate and improve how Council delivers services and positive community outcomes.
About You
  
Above all, you will be a strong leader and problem solver.
  
You will be comfortable stepping into a complex environment, understanding the different moving parts and establishing what needs to happen next. You'll know how to bring people with you through change while still being prepared to make decisions, establish expectations and hold people accountable.
  
You'll bring:
  • Proven leadership experience within government, public services or another complex community-focused organisation
  • Experience leading diverse teams and developing capability in others
  • Strong governance awareness and an understanding of working within accountable service-delivery environments
  • Demonstrated ability to turn strategy into practical programs, projects and outcomes
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
  • The confidence and political awareness to work effectively with Councillors, executives and community stakeholders
  • Strong judgement and the ability to manage competing priorities and expectations
  • Experience delivering social impact and positive community outcomes
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and willingness to challenge how things have traditionally been done
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or significant experience in a comparable leadership position.
While previous local government management experience would be advantageous, Council is prepared to consider candidates from broader government, major not-for-profit and government-funded service organisations where you have led complex community-facing programs and understand the importance of governance, accountability and measurable service outcomes.
  
This could also represent an excellent next career step for a highly capable Coordinator or senior leader from a larger, complex council environment who has the breadth of experience and leadership maturity to step into management.
  
Why Central Highlands Regional Council?
  
This is an opportunity to do more than simply inherit an established service and maintain the status quo.
  
You'll join Council at a time when important work is already underway to strengthen the foundations of the function. The opportunity for the new Manager is to build on that work, develop the team and shape how these services evolve.
There are also significant priorities ahead, including a new library strategy, cultural and creative arts strategy incorporating an increased focus on heritage, and further work on Council's Community Grants Program.
  
For someone who enjoys diversity, problem solving, change and making things better, there is a genuine opportunity to make this role your own and leave a lasting impact on both the organisation and the communities it serves.
  
The opportunity offers:
  • $210,000–$252,000 Total Remuneration Package
  • Senior leadership responsibility across a broad and diverse portfolio
  • Relocation support
  • Potential access to Council accommodation
The opportunity to live and work in the Central Highlands while making a tangible contribution to its communities.
If you are an experienced community or public service leader looking for an opportunity where you can develop people, solve complex problems, improve services and genuinely influence the future direction of a regional community, we would like to hear from you.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Sunday 13th September at 4pm

job.title: BIM / Archicad Trainer
job.description:
Design & Build are partnering with a leading Australian residential building organisation to recruit a BIM / Archicad Trainer to join their People Development function.

Based in the Hunter Region, this role will support drafting teams nationally and will involve regular travel, both interstate and nationally.

Importantly, you don't need to already be an experienced trainer.

We're equally interested in hearing from experienced Archicad 29 users, Senior Drafters, BIM specialists or technical drafting professionals who enjoy helping others and would like to pivot their career into training and development.

For the right technical person, the business is prepared to invest in your development and support you in completing your Certificate IV in Training & Assessment.

The Role
Working closely with the BIM Manager and Learning & Development team, you'll become a key technical resource supporting drafting teams across the organisation.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Delivering Archicad and BIM training to drafting teams across Australia
  • Supporting the onboarding and technical induction of new starters
  • Developing structured Archicad training programs
  • Creating training materials including guides, videos, e-learning content, job aids and SOPs
  • Running face-to-face and virtual training sessions
  • Working one-on-one and with small groups to improve technical capability
  • Identifying knowledge gaps and opportunities to improve BIM processes and training
  • Working with internal technical specialists and external BIM providers
  • Monitoring training participation and effectiveness
  • Travelling nationally to support teams across different locations
About You
There are two backgrounds we're particularly interested in:

Experienced Trainer: You may already be delivering BIM, Archicad, CAD or technical training and be looking for an opportunity within a large national organisation.

Experienced Archicad User Ready for a Career Pivot: You may be a Senior Drafter, BIM Coordinator, Archicad specialist or highly experienced residential drafting professional who loves helping others and wants to move away from day-to-day drafting into a training-focused career.
Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Strong Archicad experience – Archicad 29 highly regarded
  • A background in drafting, BIM or residential construction
  • Confidence communicating technical information in a simple way
  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills
  • An interest in coaching, mentoring and developing others
  • The ability and willingness to travel nationally
  • A proactive approach to technology and continuous improvement
  • A current driver's licence
A Certificate IV in Training & Assessment is advantageous but not essential – support can be provided to obtain this qualification for the right candidate.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is a unique opportunity to take your technical Archicad knowledge and turn it into a long-term career in training and capability development.
You'll join a major Australian building organisation, work closely with BIM and L&D specialists, gain exposure to drafting teams nationally and have the opportunity to become a recognised technical training specialist within the business.
If you're an Archicad expert who's always the person others come to for help, this could be the career pivot you've been looking for.

Apply now or contact Renee Hamilton at Design & Build Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Manager Communications & Engagement
job.description:
Manager Communications & Engagement
Central Highlands Regional Council | Emerald, QLD | Senior Leadership | Executive Package ($225-257K TRP)
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Central Highlands Regional Council to recruit a newly created Manager Communications & Engagement – an influential leadership role that will shape how Council communicates, engages and builds relationships with its communities.
  
Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this position brings together the Communications and Community Engagement functions under one dedicated leader for the first time.
  
This is an opportunity to create a more connected and consistent approach across Council, strengthening community relationships while ensuring its priorities, achievements and services are communicated clearly and effectively.
  
The Role
  
You will lead an established team of approximately eight across Communications and Community Engagement, providing the direction and structure required to successfully bring the two functions together.
  
An early priority will be helping shape Council’s new Communications Strategy while improving how community consultation is planned, captured and followed through – ensuring Council effectively closes the loop with its communities.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading Council’s strategic communications and community engagement functions
  • Developing and implementing communication and engagement strategies
  • Providing strategic advice to the CEO, Mayor and senior leadership
  • Leading community consultation and strengthening stakeholder relationships
  • Supporting Council’s Community Reference Groups and ensuring feedback is effectively actioned
  • Leading corporate communications, media relations and reputation management
  • Overseeing digital and internal communications
  • Developing the team and creating clear expectations, accountability and continuous improvement.
  
This is a highly visible position with regular interaction with the CEO, Mayor and elected members, making political awareness, sound judgement and strong relationship management critical to success.
  
About You

Council is looking for a strong communications and engagement generalist rather than a specialist in one particular discipline – someone who understands how strategic communications, media, engagement, internal communications and digital work together.
  
You will bring:
  • Senior leadership experience across communications, community and stakeholder engagement
  • Strong strategic communications, media and reputation management capability
  • Experience developing and implementing communication and engagement strategies
  • Proven people leadership and the ability to bring teams together through change
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement and influencing skills
  • The confidence and judgement to work effectively with senior executives and elected members
  • Strong political awareness and experience within government or another complex stakeholder environment
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or significant comparable leadership experience.
Experience within local or state government will be highly regarded, particularly given the political and community-facing nature of the position.
  
Why Join Central Highlands Regional Council?
  
This opportunity offers:
  • A newly created position with the opportunity to shape the function from the outset
  • Direct reporting access to the Chief Executive Officer
  • Leadership of an established Communications and Community Engagement team
  • Genuine influence over Council’s future communications and engagement strategy
  • Significant exposure to the Mayor, elected members, senior leadership and community
  • The opportunity to improve how Council engages with its communities and tells its story.
This is an opportunity to do more than manage an existing communications function. You will have the mandate to bring two areas together, establish the strategy and reshape how Council communicates and engages with the Central Highlands community.
  
Be part of something that matters, with like-minded people who truly care.
  
One Place. Many Paths. Choose Yours Here.
  
Apply Now

Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People

job.title: Capital Planning Master Scheduler
job.description:
We are looking for an experienced Capital Planning Master Scheduler to join our client on a 6-month contract, playing a key role in shaping and coordinating a long-term capital works pipeline.

This is an excellent opportunity for a strategic and highly organised capital planning professional to make a tangible impact across a complex portfolio of infrastructure, renewal, upgrade and growth projects. You will work collaboratively across the organisation to develop an integrated 10-Year Capital Works Program, helping ensure investment decisions are evidence-based, strategically aligned and deliverable.

The Opportunity
As Capital Planning Master Scheduler, you will be responsible for the development, coordination, maintenance and continuous improvement of the organisation's 10-Year Capital Works Program.

You will bring together asset management, service planning, project delivery, funding and financial considerations to establish a clear and prioritised capital investment pipeline. Your work will directly support informed decision-making, resource planning, funding advocacy and the successful delivery of infrastructure outcomes for the community.


Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading the annual development and ongoing review of the 10-Year Capital Works Program.
  • Maintaining a prioritised pipeline of renewal, upgrade, compliance and growth projects.
  • Coordinating project submissions and assessing alignment with strategic objectives.
  • Facilitating program review workshops with internal stakeholders.
  • Developing program scenarios to support funding, staging and investment decisions.
  • Establishing and maintaining an integrated master schedule covering planning, design, approvals, procurement and delivery.
  • Identifying critical paths, project dependencies, resource constraints and delivery risks.
  • Translating Asset Management Plans into long-term capital investment programs.
  • Preparing reports, dashboards and briefing papers for management, executive leadership and Council.
  • Developing capital planning databases, schedules, forecasting tools and performance reporting.
  • Providing expert advice on capital planning methodologies and prioritisation frameworks.

About Our Client
Our client is a large, community-focused local government organisation responsible for delivering a broad range of services and infrastructure to its community. Its shared community vision is centred on creating a vibrant, sustainable and prosperous future, with its current Council Plan focused on Place, People, Prosperity and Performance.

The organisation's culture is underpinned by five core values: Integrity, Courage, Openness, Respect and Excellence. These values shape how decisions are made, how people work together and how outcomes are delivered for the community.

This is an opportunity to work within a purpose-driven environment where your expertise will contribute to long-term infrastructure planning, sustainable investment and meaningful community outcomes.


Why Join?
  • 6-month contract opportunity with a significant capital planning portfolio.
  • Opportunity to influence long-term infrastructure investment and delivery.
  • Work closely with senior stakeholders across multiple service areas.
  • Make a direct contribution to community infrastructure outcomes.
  • Join an organisation committed to integrity, collaboration, innovation and excellence.

About Public Sector People
Public Sector People is a specialist Australian recruitment agency focused on the public sector, delivering permanent and temporary recruitment solutions across local, state and federal government. Our vision is to be Australia's most trusted recruitment agency, guided by our mission to do the right thing for clients, candidates, colleagues and the community. Our values are honest communication, focus, feedback and care.

job.title: MEP BIM Modeler
job.description:
BIM Modeler - Tier 1 MEP Contractor
Location: Melbourne, VIC
Salary: $110,000 - $125,000 + Super
Employment Type: Full-time
Sector: MEP / Building Services / Data Centres
 
The Opportunity
We are currently working with a leading Tier 1 MEP contractor delivering major mechanical and electrical projects across Melbourne, including complex commercial, industrial and data centre developments.
Due to continued project growth, they are looking for an experienced BIM Modeler to join their project delivery team. This is an excellent opportunity to work on technically complex projects alongside experienced engineers, project managers and construction teams.
 
The Role
As a BIM Modeler, you will be responsible for developing, coordinating and maintaining high-quality BIM models throughout the project lifecycle.
You will work closely with engineering, design, project management and site teams to ensure models accurately reflect project requirements and are suitable for construction and installation.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and maintain detailed MEP BIM models using Revit and associated modelling software.
  • Produce coordinated models and drawings for mechanical and/or electrical building services.
  • Work closely with engineers, project managers, subcontractors and site teams to resolve design and coordination issues.
  • Participate in BIM coordination and clash detection processes.
  • Review design information and identify potential constructability issues.
  • Assist with the preparation of shop drawings, fabrication information and construction documentation.
  • Maintain model accuracy and ensure deliverables meet project BIM standards and requirements.
  • Coordinate with architectural, structural and other services models.
  • Support project teams throughout design, construction and commissioning phases.
  • Contribute to BIM standards, processes and continuous improvement.
  • Attend coordination meetings and communicate modelling/design issues effectively.
About You
The successful candidate will ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a BIM Modeler within an MEP, mechanical, electrical or building services environment.
  • Strong proficiency in Revit.
  • Experience with Navisworks and clash detection/coordination.
  • Good understanding of mechanical and/or electrical building services.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings and technical documentation.
  • Experience working within a contractor, subcontractor or construction environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and an understanding of constructability.
  • Excellent communication and coordination skills.
  • Ability to work effectively within a fast-paced project environment.
Desirable Experience
Experience across any of the following would be highly regarded:
  • Data Centres / Mission Critical
  • Commercial construction
  • Industrial projects
  • High-rise developments
  • Large-scale infrastructure
  • Mechanical services
  • Electrical services
  • Fabrication modelling
  • Revit MEP
  • Navisworks Manage
Why Join?
  • Join an established Tier 1 MEP contractor.
  • Work on major, technically complex projects.
  • Exposure to some of Melbourne's largest construction and data centre developments.
  • Strong career progression into BIM Coordinator / BIM Manager positions.
  • Work alongside experienced engineering and project delivery teams.
  • Competitive salary of $110,000 - $125,000 + Super, depending on experience.
Apply
If you're an experienced BIM Modeler looking to take the next step with a leading MEP contractor, we'd like to hear from you.
Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

job.title: Principal Project Officer (Infrastructure)
job.description:
About the role
As Principal Project Officer, you will provide senior-level infrastructure, property and project expertise across the departments accommodation and infrastructure portfolio.
  
You’ll lead complex projects from planning through to delivery and close-out, while providing authoritative advice to senior leaders and stakeholders and ensuring projects meet government and departmental requirements.
  
Responsibilities
  • Lead the management and negotiation of commercial office and non-office leases and license agreements, including landlord obligations, property governance and compliance.
  • Provide authoritative advice on legislation, codes, standards, frameworks, policies and procedures relating to accommodation infrastructure.
  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of infrastructure projects and programs, including contractor management, construction and fit-out coordination, budgets, schedules, risks, stakeholder engagement and project close-out.
  • Provide strategic and timely advice to senior management and key stakeholders on infrastructure and accommodation matters.
  • Evaluate priority sites and analyse data to identify opportunities for cost efficiencies and improved accommodation strategies.
  • Develop and implement infrastructure and asset policies, procedures, standards, tools and templates that support sound decision-making and align with state wide service delivery and workforce requirements.
  • Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, service providers and other government agencies to deliver innovative infrastructure solutions.
  • Prepare high-quality project plans, briefing notes, communication plans, policies, strategies, reports and other information for a range of audiences.
  • Provide leadership, direction and support to team members to ensure projects and services are delivered efficiently, sustainably and to a high standard.
  
  
The successful candidate
You will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex infrastructure, property or accommodation projects and programs.
  • Strong knowledge and experience managing commercial leases, licenses, property obligations and governance arrangements.
  • The ability to interpret and apply legislation, standards, policies and frameworks to support sound infrastructure and property decisions.
  • Strong project management capability, including experience managing budgets, schedules, risks, contractors, construction or fit-out activities and project delivery.
  • Excellent analytical skills, with the ability to use data and evidence to identify opportunities, improve services and drive cost efficiencies.
  • Highly developed communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build productive relationships across government, industry and service providers.
  • The ability to develop practical policies, procedures, tools and strategies that support organizational and service delivery outcomes.
  • Strong leadership capability and a commitment to accountability, governance, continuous improvement and high-quality outcomes.
  • A collaborative and inclusive approach, with the ability to lead through complexity, ambiguity and change.


If you’re an experienced infrastructure or property professional with a strong background in government and additional commercial lease management experience, this is the contract opportunity for you! 

Send your application through to: daniel@publicsectorpeople.com.au & give me a call on 0466 265 446 today to discuss this opportunity in further detail!

job.title: A05 Workplace Health Safety advisor
job.description:
Public Sector People are partnering with a QLD State Government orginsation here in Brisbane who are seeking an A05 WHS officer to join their building, construction and maintenance team on a temporary contract until March 2027!

Position Description

The purpose of the Workplace Health and Safety Advisor role is to provide workplace health and safety (WHS) advice, service, and assistance to the department, including a diverse range of WHS activities and technical matter relating to building, construction and maintenance industry.
  
Here are the details of the role:
  • Role title: A05 Workplace Health & Safety
  • Pay:  $ 69.21 per hour + 12% super
  • Location: Brisbane, Canon Hill, QLD 4170
  • Start date: ASAP
  • Contract length: Initial contract until 31 March 2027 + extension
  • Hours: 38 hours per week Monday to Friday  
The role works closely with the Principal Workplace Health and Safety Advisors (PWHSA) and the WHS Manager to implement and monitor operational Workplace Heath Safety and environmental (WHS&E) matters.    
          
This role will work within a diverse team of building, construction and maintenance field and office staff.
  
Position overview:
  • Conduct site WHS&E audits and inspections to ensure compliance for both QBuild and contractor delivered work.
  • Provide WHS&E advice and guidance to department operational, supervisory and management staff regarding the departments Safety Management System (SMS) processes and requirements, and legislative compliance.
  • Assist with the development and delivery of information sessions educating on the relevant WHS&E information and activities to department staff.
  • Assist with reporting and investigating WHS&E incidents and contractor notifiable incidents.
  • Assist with the worker rehabilitation and return to work programs, under the guidance of the RRTW Advisor or WHS Manager.          
  •  Assist with coordinating with the emergency planning and response activities for offices and depots.
  • Assist with the development, review and implementation of SWMSs, risk assessments, and WHS Management plans.
  • Assist with regular WHS&E reporting for regions and business. 
  • Assist with the delivery of a range of health and safety programs, to enable a service that is responsive to the needs of the stakeholders.
Technical/operational expertise
  • Knowledge of industry, or similar industry, in order to understand the hazards, risks and control measures.
  • Ability to interpret WHS legislation, including relevant legislation, Codes of Practice, Australian Standards / International Standards, to provide advice and guidance to stakeholders.
  • Ability to build and sustain positive relationships with a range of stakeholders including employees, managers and other internal and external stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated capacity to liaise in a clear and concise manner through the use of structured written and oral communication.
Mandatory position requirements

While there are no mandatory requirements, WHS&E experience in construction, maintenance, or similar industry and Certificate IV in WHS is highly desirable

As an approved Government recruitment partner Public Sector People are ideally placed to assist you in your search for your next temporary or permanent opportunity. 

Best of luck!

We are currently working exclusively with a highly regarded Melbourne-based property developer and builder to appoint an experienced Contracts Administrator to join their in-house construction team.

An award-winning organisation that takes a fully integrated approach to property development, with architecture, interior design, construction, project management, sales, marketing, operations and asset management all managed in-house.

This is an excellent opportunity for a Contracts Administrator to join an experienced construction team and play a key role in the delivery of a multi-residential apartment development in South-East Melbourne.

Location: South-East Melbourne / CBD
Position: Contracts Administrator
Sector: Multi-Residential / Apartments
Employment: Permanent
Start: September 2026
Salary: $110,000 – $130,000 + Super

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Project Manager, you will be involved across the full project lifecycle, from pre-construction and tendering through to construction delivery and final handover.

This is a hands-on role suited to a Contracts Administrator who enjoys being involved across procurement, subcontractor management, cost control and project delivery, rather than being limited to purely administrative responsibilities.

You will work closely with the Project Manager, site team, consultants and subcontractors to ensure the project is delivered efficiently, within budget and to a high standard.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage contracts administration across the project lifecycle
  • Assist with estimating, tender preparation and subcontractor procurement
  • Prepare scopes of work, tender packages and subcontractor documentation
  • Review and compare subcontractor and supplier quotations
  • Manage subcontractor engagement, contracts and compliance
  • Review progress claims, variations and payment schedules
  • Assist with project budgeting, cost tracking and cost-to-complete forecasting
  • Monitor project costs and financial performance
  • Maintain project registers, documentation and correspondence
  • Coordinate RFIs, shop drawings, approvals and project documentation
  • Support the Project Manager and site team with day-to-day project delivery
  • Assist with subcontractor scheduling, quality inspections and defect management
  • Assist with project reporting, meetings and handover documentation
  • Ensure project documentation and compliance requirements are maintained
  • Assist with the successful delivery of key project milestones through to completion

About You
We are looking for an experienced and driven Contracts Administrator with approximately 3–5 years' experience in a construction environment.

Ideally, you will have a background delivering multi-residential or apartment developments, with experience on projects involving:
  • Basement construction
  • Approximately 5–7 storeys
  • Complex subcontractor packages
  • Tendering and procurement
  • Contracts administration
  • Cost and financial management
  • Full project lifecycle delivery

Requirements
  • 3–5 years' experience as a Contracts Administrator
  • Demonstrated experience delivering multi-residential/apartment projects
  • Relevant Diploma of Building & Construction, Construction Management or related degree
  • Strong understanding of construction methodology, contracts and project delivery
  • Strong commercial and cost management capability
  • Experience with tendering, procurement, variations and progress claims
  • Experience with CostX, Microsoft Project, Microsoft 365, Sage Intacct, BuildPass or Bluebeam will be highly regarded.

Interested?

job.title: Project Officer
job.description:
About the Role:
As Project Officer – Capital Works, you will support the delivery of a diverse portfolio of capital works and civil infrastructure projects from planning through to completion, with a strong focus on streetscape upgrades, public domain improvements, and urban revitalisation projects.

The portfolio may also include buildings, town centre upgrades, parks, roads, stormwater and other community infrastructure. You will assist with project coordination across the full project lifecycle, including design management, procurement, contract administration and construction delivery, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget and to a high standard.

The role will also involve coordinating consultants and contractors, monitoring project progress, preparing reports and documentation, supporting stakeholder engagement, and ensuring projects comply with relevant legislation, standards and Council frameworks.

Key accountabilities
  • Coordinate with internal and external project stakeholders to ensure projects are delivered on time, meet required project outcomes and deliver high quality customer service outcomes.
  • Ensure that works programs are undertaken and completed in accordance with agreed budgets, program objectives, quality measures and program timeframes, with minimal disruption to residents, businesses, pedestrians and traffic.
  • Assist with preparing tender documents and undertaking evaluation of contracts for the supply of goods and services.
  • Identify and mitigate project and program risks in relation to the, project time, cost, quality, safety, latent conditions and community consultation.
  • Ensure that the scope and status of all works is communicated effectively to all relevant internal and external stakeholders.
  • Comply with and keep abreast of any relevant legislation applicable to the performance of the duties of this position.
Essential Knowledge, Skills & Experience
  • University degree or TAFE Diploma, in civil engineering, project management, contract management or a related field or a Trades qualification or demonstrated equivalent experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to engage with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders at all levels to optimise organisational and community outcomes.
  • Demonstrated experience in the design and/or delivery of civil works using sound project management approaches, tools and understanding of project lifecycle stages.

job.title: Senior Integration and Automation Specialist
job.description:
Senior Integration & Automation Specialist

Location: Inner West, Sydney NSW
Work Type: Full Time
Hours: 35-hour week
Salary: $122,063 – $137,421 per annum, plus superannuation 12%, depending on skills, qualifications and experience.

Public Sector People are proud to be partnering with Inner West Council to appoint a Senior Integration & Automation Specialist.

This is an excellent opportunity for a hands-on technology professional to lead and mature Council’s Integration & Automation capability. Combining technical leadership with solution delivery, you’ll improve how Council’s systems connect, automate business processes and establish scalable integration practices across a complex technology environment.

This isn’t a purely architectural role. Council is looking for someone who still enjoys building – someone equally comfortable designing a solution, getting hands-on with its implementation and supporting it through to production.

The Opportunity

You’ll provide day-to-day leadership of the Integration & Automation function, with one direct report, while remaining actively involved in the design, development and support of integration and automation solutions.

Working across Microsoft Power Platform, Azure Integration Services and/or Boomi, you’ll develop APIs, automations and integrations that connect Council’s enterprise applications and improve business processes.

You’ll establish robust and reusable integration approaches across API-led, event-driven, message-based, real-time and batch integrations, while strengthening API standards, security and governance.

Working closely with business stakeholders and the Digital Service team, you’ll identify opportunities to eliminate manual processes and turn business requirements into practical, scalable solutions.

About You

You’ll be an integration and automation professional who combines strong technical capability with initiative, ownership and excellent stakeholder engagement skills.

You will bring:
  • Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate and Power Pages.
  • Enterprise integration experience using Azure Integration Services, Boomi or an equivalent platform
  • Experience designing, building, deploying and supporting production integrations and automation solutions.
  • Experience applying AI and intelligent automation to accelerate delivery and drive better business outcomes.
  • Strong knowledge of modern integration patterns and API development, management, security and governance.
  • Experience with Azure API Management or an equivalent platform.
  • Knowledge of modern integration security, including OAuth2, OpenID Connect, Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities.
  • Hands-on development capability across Python, C# or equivalent technologies, with PowerShell, JavaScript and JSON also valuable.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting capability, with the ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

A proactive approach with the confidence to work autonomously, take ownership and drive outcomes.Experience integrating TechnologyOne CiA will be highly regarded, along with exposure to platforms such as ESRI, Dynamics 365, Freshservice, Microsoft Fabric and other local government SaaS applications.

Formal management experience isn’t essential. This could suit an established technical lead or senior specialist who has mentored others, led projects or influenced stakeholders and is ready to take the next step into broader leadership.

Why Inner West Council?
  • Lead and shape Council’s growing Integration & Automation capability.
  • Remain hands-on while developing your technical and people leadership experience.
  • Work across Azure, Power Platform, TechnologyOne, APIs, data platforms and SaaS applications.
  • Establish reusable integration standards, patterns and governance practices.
  • Use automation and emerging technologies to deliver practical improvements across Council.
  • Join an organisation focused on innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.
This role will suit someone who enjoys the balance of leading and doing – a capable technical professional who can build trust across the business, take ownership of complex challenges and still enjoys getting hands-on to build solutions.

For a confidential discussion, please contact:
Esme Lynch – Principal Consultant, Public Sector People
M: 0413 282 765
E: esme@publicsectorpeople.com.au

Applications close 11:59pm, Tuesday 31st August 2026, please note Recruitment activity will commence prior to the closing date.

job.title: Tenancy Manager
job.description:
Tenancy Manager 

Our client is a well-established community housing provider delivering safe, affordable and sustainable homes across New South Wales. Their work goes beyond housing - partnering with tenants, community groups, and support services to strengthen wellbeing and build thriving communities.

They are seeking a values-driven Tenancy Manager to join their customer-focused team and play a key role in delivering exceptional tenancy management and community outcomes.

The Opportunity

In this hands-on role, you’ll be the first point of contact for tenants, ensuring their needs are met with care, professionalism and responsiveness. You’ll manage a diverse tenancy portfolio, supporting residents to sustain their housing through proactive engagement and practical problem-solving.

You’ll also work collaboratively with internal teams and external partners to address tenancy issues, manage arrears and property care, and contribute to broader community wellbeing initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide responsive, respectful and consistent customer service
  • Manage tenancy agreements in line with the NSW Residential Tenancies Act 2010
  • Support tenants to sustain their tenancies through early intervention and engagement
  • Manage arrears, property standards, and anti-social behaviour
  • Prepare documentation and represent the organisation at NCAT where required
  • Collaborate with colleagues and support partners to achieve positive tenant outcomes
  • Maintain accurate records and comply with organisational policies and reporting standards
About You

You’re an organised and empathetic professional who thrives in a busy, people-focused environment. You bring a mix of practical tenancy management skills and a genuine commitment to community impact.

Essential:
  • Experience in property management (community housing, public housing, or real estate)
  • Sound understanding of the NSW Residential Tenancies Act 2010
  • Strong communication, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills
  • Self-motivated, with the ability to work autonomously and as part of a team
  • Current NSW Driver’s Licence
Desirable:
  • Understanding of social and affordable housing frameworks
  • Experience engaging with vulnerable communities
  • Prior NCAT representation experience
  • Qualifications in social work, community services or a related discipline
What’s on Offer
  • Salary: $95,000 + Super + Salary Packaging (SCHADS Level 4)
  • Hybrid working model (4 days onsite / 1 day WFH)
  • Supportive, values-led culture focused on inclusion and empowerment
  • Opportunity to make a tangible difference in people’s lives and communities
If you’re a housing professional who combines a business head with a social heart, this role offers a meaningful opportunity to make a lasting impact.
